chosen_option_text: “We cannot possibly let this go ahead!” spits your eternally-angry Chief of Enforcement Ashley Bourdain, clutching her fists tighter by the second. “Blocking those gorgeous views of Vanilla Llama City is bad enough, but boasting such obnoxious disrespect for our glorious government is nothing short of treason! Any building, or billionaire for that matter, to purposefully inconvenience you ought to be judged more damningly than to simply call them ‘spiteful’. Give my team the nod and I’ll have any eyesore you want demolished or hubristic billionaire arrested before sundown.”

title: Let Them Eat Rainbow Cake!
text: When high-profile lesbian celebrity Ellen Lynch was asked to leave popular establishment The Vanilla Llama City Diner, it was made clear to her that this was because she was dining with her lesbian partner. The restaurant owners refused to serve the homosexual couple, citing a conflict with their religious beliefs. This isn’t the first time something like this has been flagged by the press, but Lynch is keen to make some noise.
chosen_option_text: The Deputy Mayor of Vanilla Llama City, Cillian Shaft strides in, dashingly pink trench coat flapping in the breeze behind him. “The mayor won’t like this, but if we want Vanilla Llama to be a prestigious and progressive nation on the world stage, we’ve got to go even further! To cater for... that is to protect the rights of the gay community, we should establish zones in each restaurant or other service industry venture that are reserved exclusively for gay and lesbian people. Think of our standing in the international gay community! Think of the tourism! We’d be a shining beacon for gay culture!”

title: Much Ado About Abortion
text: A monstrous debate between pro-life and pro-choice groups has erupted after a high-profile case of a pregnant woman aborting her foetus because she ‘didn’t feel like it’ hit the tabloids.
chosen_option_text: “Abortion has to be legal if we’re going to last as a nation,” says Brynlee Windass, President of the Society of Bitter Old People. “Have you ever thought that with our nation’s growing population of 56 million, we soon aren’t going to be able to squeeze any more people into Vanilla Llama? If we use abortion to control the population, we’ll make great savings and can spend the money elsewhere. One child per family should just about do it I think. Extraneous ones can be sold to other countries.”

title: Dangerous Liaisons
text: Your brother just broke up with his most recent girlfriend. However, this one turned out to be a bit different from all his previous love interests.
chosen_option_text: “Although I agree with your brother’s diagnoses, I disagree with his method of rehabilitation,” states Milo Guterres, a psychiatrist, as he beckons your brother to a leather couch. “Serial stalkers are known to have mental disorders that increase their infatuation with the object of their desire, leading to irrational and anti-social behaviour. Prison time will not cure them. What they need is an extensive course of cognitive behavioural therapy, where they will learn to decode, process, and alter their warped thinking patterns.”

title: Compulsory Gun Ownership?
text: This weekend, a citizen’s group calling itself Gun Owners of Vanilla Llama has petitioned Congress with a controversial bill making gun ownership compulsory.
chosen_option_text: “While the Gun Owners of Vanilla Llama have the safety and security of our people in mind, it would simply be impractical to enforce,” comments Police Chief Kellyanne Harrison. “A better option would be to legalize, and encourage use of, concealed carry laws, which would allow responsible citizens to keep firearms with them at all times, on their person, to kill any wacko or their cousin who they think is threatening them.”

title: Some People Never Listen
text: Two senior officials caught having affairs, five separate expenses scandals and the leaking of top-secret plans for the Cabinet Secretary’s birthday party is usually more than enough to cover in one public announcement. You were therefore surprised to find that another issue altogether has caught the public’s attention: activists representing the nation’s deaf and hearing-impaired communities have taken you to task over the lack of a Vanilla Llaman Sign Language interpreter at your public addresses.
chosen_option_text: “Being deaf doesn’t have to be an impairment, so don’t make it one,” signs activist Bongani Coleman, adding a few more vulgar hand gestures that you are sure aren’t official sign language. “Having an interpreter is the least you could do. Deaf people in Vanilla Llama are subject to a harmful mix of preconceptions and ignorance, so it’s about time you listened to us. Perhaps you could also establish a national ‘Deaf Awareness Week’ to celebrate the contributions deaf people have made to society, and to persuade organisations and individuals to bear us in mind.”

title: Gone Girls
text: All of Vanilla Llama has been desperate for news of Amelie Adams, a Vanilla Llaman teenager who went missing yesterday. Search parties have been gathered, rivers are being dredged, and thermal-camera-wielding helicopters are scouring every inch of the nation. As you receive another hourly update on ‘Amazing Amelie’, a Bigtopian mother approaches you with a tear-soaked picture.
chosen_option_text: “Look, I’m no racist,” booms Nomfundo Bowie, Grand Supreme High Dude of local ‘group of friends’ Blanking Big-Nosed Bigtopians, adjusting her conspicuously pointed white hood. “But we all know those types: criminals! Don’t let them abuse government resources just because they can’t control their kids. Everyone knows they all wind up as hardened thugs — jaywalking, listening to aggressive Bigtopian music, selling authentic Northern Vanilla Llaman headgear without a permit... Scum! These bigwig kids are just out of control. Mark them all down as the runaways they are and get back to the real victims: the innocent Vanilla Llaman doves like Amazing Amelie.”

title: Animation Provocation
text: When media boss Ian Tivruski green-lighted a new Brancalandian animated series for the Vanilla Llaman Kids Network, he thought he was commissioning a delightful children’s show about metal-working amazons who knit cozy jumpers for their grandkids. As it turns out, the surprisingly explicit animation Sword Heroins: Love Needle has caused a lot of confusion amongst young viewers, and upset many parents.
chosen_option_text: “I think we’re ignoring a broader issue here,” bemoans frustrated animator Parker Stonetrey, “which is that animated art forms are never taken seriously enough to be considered anything more than kiddie fare. I say that we develop Vanilla Llama’s artistic vision and creativity by subsidising adult animation. When people think Vanilla Llama, they should think hentai!”

title: All That Glitters
text: When a celebrity power couple like pro-footballer Bruno Green and fashion model and former pop starlet Prudence Mulder marries, there’s bound to be some glitz and glamour. In fact, thanks to Prudence’s obsession with being a “fairytale princess” the beachside wedding also involved many tonnes of glitter, which is now drifting across the nearby lagoon, raising an important question — what about the mess?
chosen_option_text: “Awww but the glitter is LUVVERLY,” coos the blushing bride, her ultra-thin arms flapping as they catch a weak breeze. “We should make all the beaches and streets look all pretty and glittery, innit? It’d be so nice, and everyone would be smiling all the time because... because... AWWW I LOVE GLITTER, ME!”

title: Short Shorts Too Short?
text: Dress codes for young women are in the news again after a violent clash between parents on opposite sides of the issue. The ringleaders have been dragged into your office by your Minister of Education for an impromptu arbitration and time-out.
chosen_option_text: Finally, fifteen year old Samus sits down at your desk, barely looking at you while she types vigorously at her smartphone. “Jeez, like, get off my back. I can, like, wear whatever I want. Boys are so stupid sometimes. Look at these shorts; they’re even patriotic!” She stands up and does a twirl to show her short shorts are in your national colours with Vanilla Llama emblazoned across the backside. “Pretty nice right?” She smacks her gum loudly, takes a selfie, and goes back to texting.

title: A Timely Intervention
text: You and your cabinet are on a tour of the nearby Vanilla Llama Watch Factory, which has long been famous throughout all of Land of Faceplace. The poor state of the factory — and its rapidly declining sales figures, carelessly left on the manager’s desk — are clear for all to see. Shuffling by your side, the manager sighs: “Leader, we’ve had some tough years here. But we don’t know what to do to bring the good days back.”
chosen_option_text: “The hour is at hand! This is the time of Violet!” shouts Violetist priest Paul Thawne through an open window. “The time spent watching these evil little machinations would be better spent praising the almighty Violet! We must rid ourselves of this factory of evil, seeking and burning all its offspring; wherever it may hide in our land! Violet demands that the government ban and destroy every horological horror, for — as is written in the texts — there is no reason or rhyme, no meaning or time but by Violet’s dread love!” The priest tries to light a match but is dragged away by your bodyguards.

title: O Fortuna!
text: JACKPOT! It seemed impossible, it seemed unlikely, it seemed as if the odds would not favour you. Yet you, Leader, are the lucky winner of a major cash prize from last night’s national lottery, thanks to that lottery ticket your mother had gifted you for Maxxmas. Yet before you can even celebrate, you realize that your good fortune has made national headlines.
chosen_option_text: “Did mommy dear put your name on the lottery ticket? No? Good!” exclaims your brother while unceremoniously snatching the fortuitous piece of paper from your hand. “Just say that the ticket was mine, and all you’ll have to deal with is a few angry stares for a while. You’ve dealt with worse! This way, our family will be happy, all thanks to the numbers 4, 8, 15, 16, 23, and 42. But don’t worry, if you ever lose your office, your dear, old brother will take care of you...”

title: Pure Madness
text: Purity balls have become the latest craze among some social conservatives in Vanilla Llama, with many sexual abstinence groups endorsing a ceremony where teenage girls promise to remain chaste until they get married, wearing a ring as a token of that promise. Feminist groups, however, have denounced this practice.
chosen_option_text: “This is patriarchy at its worst!” yells women’s rights advocate Samde Duras, author of critical thesis Purity: A History of Ball-Holding in Vanilla Llama. “I can’t bear to see any more photos of adolescent girls wearing wedding gowns, pledging their chastity to fathers dressed as bridegrooms. These men seem to think they own their daughters’ bodies, to be transferred to their sons-in-law! Look, Leader, I don’t care if a woman wants to remain a virgin until she gets married, but these purity balls objectify women and should be banned.”

title: Market Crash
text: On a busy Saturday morning, a minicab driver took a shortcut through a crowded market street. After skidding on some banana peels, he lost control and crashed through a dozen fruit and vegetable stalls, narrowly avoiding injuring anyone. Pedestrians are donning full body armor, and Vanilla Llamen are beginning to accept that reckless driving and speeding in the inner city may be just another fact of life.
chosen_option_text: “Why don’t you just pedestrianise a big chunk of the city centre?” suggests tourist Simon Turner, adjusting his anti-smog facemask. “It’ll make the whole area much prettier, quieter and cleaner, and it’ll let you show off the beauty of the heart of the city.”

title: This Green and Pleasant Land
text: Good news, everyone! An unexpected rise in the water table has transformed a million acres of former desert into green and fertile and farming-ready land. As the government owns this land, it’s now up to you what you do with it.
chosen_option_text: “Excuse me, is anyone going to ask why this has happened?” asks party-pooping scientist Ming Holt. “We can’t make use of this land till we understand what happened. I suggest establishing a research station here, and getting a better understanding of the ecological changes that led to this fertile land emerging.”

title: Is There an Election in Marche Noire or Are You Just Happy to See Us?
text: Facing a tight political race at home, Otto Kratt, the authoritarian leader of Marche Noire, and his cronies plan to clinch his fourth reelection by campaigning for the votes of Marche Noirian emigrants in Vanilla Llama. Alarmed and angered by his many flagrant violations of human rights, socially-conscious protestors have demanded that you forbid him from propagating his vitriolic views on Vanilla Llaman soil in order to hamper his chances of victory.
chosen_option_text: “Putrid lies!” howls Sierra Prefect, a supportive Marche Noirian immigrant carrying a life-size cardboard cutout of Otto Kratt. “We love Otto Kratt! He is the most wonderful and glorious leader of Marche Noire who cares deeply for us when he chooses. He has every right to talk to his kinsmen wherever they are! You keep saying that people here have freedom of speech, yet you would deprive our ruler of his freedom to speak to us now? Leader, you must allow Mr. Kratt to campaign and organize rallies here.”

title: Imitation Station
text: While chauffeuring you to work this morning, your driver notified you of a recent spike in motorized vehicle accidents. He says that the cause is several distracting radio advertisements - one ironically telling drivers to “buckle up”. These ads include sounds of screams, screeching tyres, honking horns, and police sirens, causing confusion for drivers on the road.
chosen_option_text: “Whoa, whoa, whoa, let’s slow down here, people,” says grumpy middle-aged woman Vera Kimmel. “There is an incredibly easy solution here, and that’s just to not allow radios or any other audio systems in cars. Think about it! No more young drivers ‘sharing’ the latest chart tunes at full volume as they drive through town centres, no more screaming toddlers demanding that nursery rhymes are on endless loop on long car journeys and no more sad songs making you want to take a hard left into oblivion when you’re driving along the clifftop. Wait, is that one just me?”

title: Subpar Suburbs
text: A water main burst in a suburb of Vanilla Llama City. After months of inaction, the pool of standing water has turned the now largely abandoned commercial district into a watering hole for local wildlife. Local businesses have come to you demanding change.
chosen_option_text: “Every one of these plans conveniently forgets about the animals,” chastises the head barista from Bean Me Up Coffee. “Y’all saunter in here after mother nature has made the best of a bad situation. That watering hole is crucial to the local wildlife, and it simply isn’t fair to take that away from the bunnies and deer and the cute little birds. Let’s take whatever money we were going to waste on rebuilding this failing town and turn it into a nature reserve.”

title: Skin’s the Wrong Colour
text: One of your nephews decided to go under the needle, and cover half of his body in a veritable panoply of tattoos depicting various scenes from a number of Nicolas Cage movies. As a result, he was fired from his job as a school receptionist.
chosen_option_text: Your nephew, flexing his arm to make Ghost Rider and H. I. McDunnough dance with each other, complains to you: “This is nothing less than obvious discrimination! I was excelling at my job, had Employee of the Month three times running, my colleagues said I was a kick-ass national treasure. But as soon as I got all inked up, my job was stolen from me, gone in sixty seconds, given away to my assistant Mandy. There goes my job at Ridgemont High! You have to stop businesses from discriminating against those who want to express themselves. In fact, you have to protect the rights of free expression and bodily autonomy, and make sure that nobody ever is discriminated against for what they choose to write or draw on their body. You know, it could happen to anyone, it could happen to you.”

title: Marriage by Proxy Server
text: After an online petition that would allow people to legally be married over the internet reached over one million signatures last night, you awake to find your inbox inundated with emails and a crowd of petitioners waiting inside your office, all demanding you take action.
chosen_option_text: “Oh, that’s a terrible idea!” chides your nettling aunt. “You have to be careful on the internet. You never know if the people you’re talking to really are who they say they are. Why just the other day, I was being courted by this youthful hunk of a gentleman on MatchMakers. But, when we finally met in person, the scoundrel was as old and flabby as me! It just goes to show that some things like dating and marriage should only be done offline and in person.”

title: The Lowest Form of Wit
text: Kamehameha Watson, your Minister of Health, became a target of criticism when he responded to a political opponent’s colorful insults by saying “Maybe you should consider rinsing your dirty mouth with bleach. It might even help you get rid of that bad breath.” Unfortunately, some citizens took this as actual advice that this would work as a treatment for their own stinky exhalations, and have been hospitalized with painful injuries.
chosen_option_text: “Look, it is not my problem that some people in this country aren’t the sharpest knives in the drawer,” sneers Watson, throwing his arms up in exasperation. “Sarcasm, people! It shouldn’t be so hard to understand. Even my 5-year-old niece got the joke. I guess the proles must be so adept at comprehending rhetorical devices because of our robustly funded education system, and you DON’T need to spend more on that. That was me being sarcastic again, in case you missed it. Yeesh.”

title: Cheerleading Community Does the Splits
text: When East Vanilla Llama City High School denied a male student’s request to join their cheerleading squad, they thought that was the end of it. Since then, the story has been picked up by the national media, with the boy, the cheerleading coach, and a spokesperson from Equality Vanilla Llama giving interviews about the controversy. Now, a gaggle of highly-opinionated and very-spirited individuals have entered your office, demanding your attention.
chosen_option_text: “Give me an ‘E’! Give me a ‘Q’! Give me a ‘U’-‘A’-‘L’! Give me an ‘I’, and a ‘T’, and a great big ‘Y’! What’s it spell? EQUALITY!” cries Dawa Barker, doing an impressive backflip routine in his plaid skirt. “Every boy deserves an equal chance to live out their dreams, whether that dream is to cheer a mediocre football team, or be on a mediocre football team! You must force every school to allow any individual to join any team they want, regardless of sex! Why not? Girls are just as strong as boys, and we boys can be darn cute in these skirts!” Cheering your name, he cartwheels out the door.

title: Going Off the Rails
text: With suicide-by-train incidents in Vanilla Llama’s stations becoming disturbingly common, commuters and rail operators are irritated by the impact on their day-to-day activities.
chosen_option_text: “People who try to kill themselves shouldn’t be punished for being ill, and neither should the families of victims of suicide,” your Minister of Health, Gene Tolkien, entreats passionately. “Being suicidal is often a sign of mental illness or depression, and our government mustn’t stoop to punishing families for having sick relatives. We ought to focus on suicide prevention rather than hounding these families for money, and we would save a lot of lives through education and extending a helping hand to those who need our support.”

title: Have Your Cake and Don’t Eat It
text: Sydney Pugwash, a young dancer, recently collapsed with the complications of what was revealed to be anorexia nervosa while dancing in the small, televised role of ‘Girl Waiting for Pater Maxxmas’. National attention has now been drawn to the growing prevalence of eating disorders and related hospitalizations in Vanilla Llama, especially among the dance community.
chosen_option_text: “Here’s some food for thought,” says psychologist Des Carter, handing you a copy of his new book Cogeato Ergo Sum: I Eat, Therefore I Am. “Eating disorders are growing year on year, in both male and female Vanilla Llamen. They may be the result of low self-esteem, body dysmorphia, or can be comorbid with other psychological disorders. Due to the high morbidity, it is vital that you subsidize psychiatric in-patient treatment and prevent future eating disorders by encouraging citizens to attend government funded therapy. Now, why don’t you lie down on this couch and tell me how you feel...”

title: A Right Not to Work?
text: High ranking officials and devout followers of a major religion have requested that the government close down retail stores during their weekly holy day, in accordance with their religious views.
chosen_option_text: Slacker freelance food reviewer Adele McDuck, still in pajamas and eating a pizza slice on a ratty couch, sends you a video chat invitation. “Dude, why not just give everybody shorter work weeks? Make flex time, telecommuting, and 35-hour work weeks mandatory for all us working folk. Trust me, the people will love you for it man!”

title: A Game Theory
text: A new study performed in East Vanilla Llama City High School showed a major increase in student engagement when video games were added to lessons. A gaggle of laptop-wielding citizens stand in your office, debating the role of video games in education.
chosen_option_text: The nephew you’re babysitting looks up from his tablet and babbles, “Know what I think? We should be playing games we actually like in school. BloxCraft taught me how to build things and be creative, and Furlough taught me friendship and teamwork! Give us some class time where we can play whatever video games we want. The teacher can even play too! That way we learn stuff and have fun! Oh, and I promise I won’t say naughty words when I die this time!”

title: The Deportation of Mr. B. Leeper
text: Brancalandian pop star Bryan Leeper has gotten into trouble with the law yet again while on tour in Vanilla Llama. He was caught urinating on a fire hydrant, making this his tenth arrest in the past year. Tens of thousands of anti-Bleepers have signed a petition demanding that the pop star be deported back to his native Brancaland.
chosen_option_text: “We don’t want the little brat back!” declares the Brancalandian Foreign Minister, seen smashing Bryan Leeper CDs with a hockey stick. “I bumped into the Maxtopian ambassador on my way here. It seems that Mr. Leeper has an outstanding legal issue over in Maxtopia that could involve jail time if he’s found guilty. Why not extradite him there as a diplomatic move? What’s that? Well yes, Maxtopia has the death penalty. I’m sure he hasn’t done anything that serious there.”

title: The Artwork in the Attic
text: After the death of the wealthy Maxtopian immigrant Emmeline Judi Webster,  a large stash of paintings, many of which are believed to have been produced by the most notable artists in the history of Maxtopia, was found in her attic.  With no will to reference, it is up to the government to decide what should be done with the discoveries.
chosen_option_text: “Pay to see them!” gasps Grogu Laine, the Maxtopian Minister of Culture and part-time art critic. “There are paintings of great historical and cultural value to my country in that collection!  They should be returned to Maxtopia with all due haste!  Just imagine ‘The Fall of St. Barrysburg’ hanging on the walls of the Maxtopian town house of Wilhelm Ruff, as the noises of war reached his ears from outside his study.  Does it not stir your soul?”

title: Wiggle Room
text: A curious new weight loss fad has wormed its way into the world of fat slimming in Vanilla Llama — deliberate self-infection with tapeworms.
chosen_option_text: “Let’s not open this can of worms too hastily,” cautions Cortana Kettering, a nerdy researcher from prominent pharmaceutical company Mhizer, as she flips through a thick clipboard containing colourful charts and coffee stains. “There’s been plenty of research into the risks and rewards of using tapeworms to lose weight, and there’s a pretty clear conclusion — it sucks, and we’re not referring to lost body weight. But, guess what? Thanks to rigorous trials conducted by yours truly, Mhizer’s approved weight loss pills can help you burn up to 10% of your body fat in a year without too much risk! It’s true, many consumers can’t afford conventional methods of losing weight, so you should subsidise the production of our wonder pills to give everyone the equal opportunity they deserve.”

title: Democracy Going to the Dogs?
text: After a recent election installed a small dog as a member of parliament, the fringe group “Brains for Ballots” has demanded for the government to tighten voting restrictions.
chosen_option_text: “Umm... huh?” inquires village idiot Peter Wildish. “I voted? When? Oh, yeah. Please don’t make me not vote. The ballots are really tasty, and where else would I get my fibre? Everyone should have the right to vote, no matter what their favourite greenhouse is! Then we can all get the government to do what we want! First thing I think we should do is, uh, ban fruit? I hate fruit.”

title: Mal Appetit!
text: Hugh Jass, Vanilla Llama’s most famous TV foodie, drew a lot of criticism when he visited a world-class restaurant in yesterday’s episode and gorged on expensive gourmet foods in a manner that some viewers found too “appetite-stimulating.” Mr. Jass’ extravagance was said to be particularly disrespectful to millions of poor Vanilla Llaman citizens who could not afford one of the dishes he ate with their entire monthly salary.
chosen_option_text: “Mon dieu!” grumbles Mr. Jass, sniffing his croissant, and throwing it away untouched. “Do these wretched ignorami not recognise the worth of a good tagliolini con tartufo? ‘Pasta with mushrooms’ indeed! If these peasants have neither the means nor aspiration to appreciate vicarious high-quality culinary culture, they can simply change the channel. I render a valuable service to our economy by giving publicity to our first-class restaurants. So, how about the government picks up the restaurant bills for our gastronomic journalism? I’ll cover the service charge, of course.”

title: Burn! Burn Everything!
text: A recent anti-government rally by highly disgruntled teens has brought a previously minor issue to the fore: should people be permitted to burn Vanilla Llama’s flag, or should it be a crime?
chosen_option_text: “These barbarians are suggesting burning the flag of our glorious nation as if it were a piece of scrap cloth! First it’s burning the flag, and before you know it, it’s rebellion and anarchy!” Kathryn Edwards scowls. “Flag burning should be punishable by a good flogging!”

title: Operation Failed
text: Dr. Henri Jacquil made the headlines yesterday after a mistake made during a routine operation caused the death of your Minister of Foreign Affairs. With the recent advances in the capabilities of artificial intelligence, some in the medical field are wondering if autonomous robot surgeons should be given a whack at surgery.
chosen_option_text: “Why stop at just the operating room doors when there’s so much more an AI could do for us?” asks Dr. Elizabeth Kamen, Professor of Experimental Gynaecological Robotics, fetching a fresh box of batteries from the top shelf. “We could make hospitals so much more efficient if we allowed them to adopt more roles: diagnostic chatbots, robot nurses, computerised counsellors, and so on. AIs should outnumber humans by at least twenty to one on the hospital staff.”

title: Foetal Furore
text: Video coverage of a protest outside of an abortion clinic has gone viral after the footage indicated that pro-life campaigners prevented ingress of pregnant women, causing the patients visible distress. In response, the Womyn’s Liberation League has pushed for a bill that it says would protect access to clinics.
chosen_option_text: “What about the right to free speech?” pleads Yoshi Ratican, lawyer for the pro-life activists depicted in the footage. “These are public spaces, and my clients should have the freedom, as well as the ability, to get their views across. You may disagree with them, but it would be draconian for the government to prohibit their citizens from revealing to people the truth about any medical procedure they are getting.”

title: Flooding the Market
text: Recent floods devastated low-lying areas, and the affected areas are only just starting to recover. Now, news is emerging that during the disaster many local retailers were found to have significantly elevated prices for basic necessities such as water, blankets, flashlights, and matsutake mushrooms.
chosen_option_text: “Power to the People! Potatoes for the Proletariat!” chants pro-communalist speaker Nefertiti Simpson, whose father is said to own half of Emu County. “I ask you, why isn’t the government mass-producing and storing long-life foodstuffs, in order to distribute them for free during times of crisis and national emergency?”

title: The One-Trick Pony
text: Secretariat, a horse recently elected as mayor of Emu City, has been vetoing every single bill coming into his office, sternly shouting “Neigh!” every time.
chosen_option_text: “Meow!” trills Ms. Snuggleworth, pushing off all the papers on your desk aside from a bill proposing her ‘Animal Personhood (Except Icky Dogs)’ agenda be made policy nationwide. Purring persuasively, she curls up in your lap.

title: Everyone Loves Shipping
text: Since their invention, globally standardised shipping containers have been critical to facilitating international trade, allowing for the easy transfer of goods between different modes of transport. However, for some time Vanilla Llama has had a strongly negative trade balance — that is, it imports far more than it exports. This has led to a domestic surplus of these containers, with thousands of the steel boxes endlessly accumulating outside ports and freight terminals.
chosen_option_text: “Nobody is coming to pick these containers up, so we need to fill them, and filling them means fixing that trade deficit,” counsels business analyst Brett Onwards, who has spent all morning trying to sell homemade cookies to your staff. “We need to re-gear our economy towards manufacturing and export production. That means using subsidies to push these industries up, funded with tariffs on imported goods. As the trade balance corrects, our metal mountain will move offshore.”

title: Video Games Too Violent, Say Parents
text: Recently, there has been an enormous commercial success for ‘violent’ video games such as ‘Blood ‘n’ Guts 2: The Revenge’, ‘Tremor’, and ‘Grand Theft Tricycle’. Several parents’ groups have been calling for tougher restrictions on these games.
chosen_option_text: “Why not rate games the same way we rate movies?” asks Norman Larkin, a spokesperson for the Vanilla Llama Censorship Board. “We could give each game a content rating based on age appropriateness, and add descriptors on the box explaining why the game gets a certain rating. A little funding and we can stop children getting violent video games without affecting all the older ‘gamers’. Everyone will be happy. Except tax payers, I guess.”

title: You’ve Got a Friend in Bee
text: Honeybee populations have been decreasing at an alarming rate, according to a recent study published in Not That Popular Science magazine. Experts have swarmed your office demanding you take action or face catastrophic consequences.
chosen_option_text: “Whatever happened to leaving nature alone?” queries the eccentric ‘Doctor Bees’, carrying suitcases buzzing with bees and seen wearing a full bee costume. “More bee colonies? Pesticides? Genes? Buzz off! Have you ever stopped to think that we are to blame for this mess? Why don’t we free the bees and let nature take its course? Sure, the beekeeping industry would suffer, but if we do nothing the alternative is total environmental disaster! Buzz buzz buzz!”

title: Born to Be My Baby
text: When Moiraine Rose and her husband couldn’t conceive, they employed a surrogate to bear a child for them, using the father’s sperm and the surrogate mother’s egg. However, after the baby was born, the surrogate mother refused to give up the child and is battling for permanent custody.
chosen_option_text: “That’s a terrible idea. Nobody should put baby in a corner!” grumbles RuPaul Franco, the director of Vanilla Llama City Minimum Security Orphanarium, cradling a baby in his arms, while two other toddlers clutch at his clothes. “Our institution is overflowing with poor orphans. Wouldn’t it be better if you just provided financial incentives, perhaps paid for with a small tax increase, for infertile couples to adopt?” Taking advantage of your momentary absent-mindedness, he puts the baby on your lap. “Speaking of adoption, would you like to take care of this adorable little girl? I think she likes you.”

title: A Midsummer Night’s Snooze-Fest
text: As legions of interns scramble to set up a stage in your office, your Minister of Theatrics dramatically announces that her Ministry has organized a play for you. The play purportedly tells a tragic story: the public apathy toward the long-dead but highly-influential Vanilla Llaman playwright Bill Wakesword.
chosen_option_text: An intern apparently playing the part of ‘unenthusiastic teenager’ pokes the Minister with a smartphone, causing him to crumble to the floor in mock agony. The intern robotically states, “Alas. Poor Wakesword. I knew him well. I would have surely been willing to get interested in Wakesword if his word choice was easier. If only we could rework Wakesword so that it appealed to me, a disaffected teenager, and my social media habits.”

title: Licensing Driving Vanilla Llamen Crazy
text: Your cousin arrived at your office this afternoon, out of breath and deeply frustrated at having to spend day after day filling out forms, only to wait for six hours in a queue to register for another appointment to receive his 27B/6 form to finalize his registration and legally drive the sweet new ride he bought six weeks ago. You’ve agreed, after some persuasion, to hold a meeting with your Minister of Transportation and other experts to look into streamlining the process.
chosen_option_text: “I have a radical idea,” announces Yolanda Schultz, the CEO of Vanilla Llama’s largest automobile manufacturer. “Simply license car dealerships to handle these processes for consumers! We can fill out all the necessary insurance paperwork for car owners, and even issue driving permits! The DMV is only slow because it has no competition. If dealerships can compete with one another for the best service, buying and registering a new car won’t be such a frustrating ordeal!”

title: “Partisanship Too Far?” Wrongly Asks Opposition
text: After a recent incident where a lifeguard refused to save a drowning swimmer because she thought he looked like he belonged to another political party, talking heads on cable TV have seized upon the moment to ask if the current partisan political tensions in Vanilla Llama have gotten out of control.
chosen_option_text: “I don’t see what the problem is,” notes your aide, turning off your TV. “In fact, I say we enhance partisan identification by designating what colors people can wear based on their political affiliation. Then you’ll immediately know who is working to better the country, and who only has morally bankrupt and wrongheaded ideas.”

title: Parliamentary Playground
text: After a WhoTube video featuring MPs in an outright brawl went viral, foreign commentators now regularly mock the hijinks in the Vanilla Llaman Parliament. In order to save face, several MPs have tried to rein in the legislature’s embarrassing behavior.

title: Siren Song

title: Jolly Roger Sighted Off the Port Bow!

title: A Capital City for Vanilla Llama?

text: Mobs of disgruntled employees picket fast-food chains across Vanilla Llama, tossing cheeseburgers at customers and burning their uniforms — all in the name of dignity and fairer wages.

title: Warning, Fatigue
text: A recent midnight explosion at the Vanilla Llaman National Steelworks, which claimed nine lives and injured a dozen more, was found to be due to an easily fixable error. title: Famous Rapper Going South?

title: A Dread Letter

title: Bet Your Life

title: Betting on the Future

title: Fake News, Everyone!

title: Let Freedom Ring

title: Nazi Sympathizers Plan Rally

title: Parking Hell
text: The new director of the Vanilla Llama City Department of Transportation has suggested that imposing dynamic parking prices might help ease the city centre’s nightmarish congestion. Because the national government owns large parts of the capital, the plan cannot proceed without your approval.

title: A Question of Bad Faith
text: The Movementarians, the infamous cult associated with a mass suicide in the United Federation, has expressed interest in purchasing a vacant plot of land in Vanilla Llama. title: A Blast From the Past
text: A teacher and four schoolchildren were killed on a field trip in a remote region of Vanilla Llama after an old anti-personnel mine was accidentally detonated. The landmines - relics of the nation’s previous wars - have taken the lives of many over the years.

title: Stop Training and Start Coaching
text: A feasibility study into railway lines in the boondocks of Vanilla Llama has suggested that they are economically unsustainable. title: Vanilla Llama Falls Flat in Singing Contest
text: Last night, in the finals of popular reality TV contest Land of Faceplacevision, the Vanilla Llaman representative lost, despite giving what almost all critics in Vanilla Llama have declared to be a superior performance. title: Support Your Local Arms Manufacturer
text: After the Conglomerated Vanilla Llaman Arms Syndicate announced yet another setback in the development of a promised new fighter jet, the Hell-Emu 3000, the Ministry of Defense is considering the previously unthinkable: importing from overseas.

title: Citizens Struggle Under “Unfair” Tax Burden

title: Maternity Leave a Must, Say Mothers

title: Toss the Coin?
text: A recent financial crisis has seen the currency of East Lebatuck plummet, making that nation a popular holiday destination for Vanilla Llamen. chosen_option_text: “If you allow this fraud to continue, I’ll go bankrupt!” yells Agnes Rogers, the owner of the Eckie-Cola Company, emptying her pockets and scattering dozens of East Lebatuckese coins on your desk. “These marauders have come back from holiday and literally plundered our coin-operated vending machines. title: Opening the Door to Controversy
text: Actor Piers Hill, the famously tweedy star of superhero franchise Superbloke, has been heavily criticised after an incident at a Shop-Qwik, in which he was accused of “holding back women’s rights by holding open doors”.

title: Loose Lips, Characters Shipped?
text: In what has become the latest cultural controversy to strike Vanilla Llama, the highly anticipated series finale of the long-running fantasy cartoon show Time Adventure saw two of the protagonist’s main male companions share a brief, romantic kiss, confirming a decade’s worth of rumors surrounding their relationship. title: Your Wild Self(ie)
text: A nature photographer on assignment in the Kawandalandian wilderness caught an emu toying with their spare camera equipment. Either on purpose or by accident, this emu managed to snap a selfie. chosen_option_text: “Whether Vanilla Llaman or beast, we are promoting a culture of selfishness and unchecked narcissism,” complains self-styled intellectual and motivational speaker Kanya Putin. “I don’t know where this is going to lead us, but it won’t be anything good. title: Hush... Hush, Sweet Charlotte
text: Your personal assistant, Charlotte Sweet, has threatened to tell the newspapers you had an affair with her unless you give her lots of money.
chosen_option_text: “Maybe this little problem really isn’t a dilemma,” opines your press advisor, August Warner. “We live in modern times, and I don’t think the public care about who sleeps with whom. You’re better off seizing the initiative and telling the world about every relationship you’ve had in a series of memoirs. Make it juicy enough to be exciting, and at the very least people will say you’re honest. People don’t say that a whole lot about politicians these days.”

title: Child’s Play
text: When bored Brancalandian schoolchild Otohime Ephron was playing on her computer, she accidentally found her way into the Vanilla Llama Armed Forces Internal Database. While playing, she promoted a janitor to Admiral of the Fleet, sent the warmongering General William Lovegood to bombard the Skandilundian border with two dozen tanks and changed the military’s motto to ‘Otohime Rulez 4eva’.
chosen_option_text: “This little brat has cost us hundreds of manhours of work fixing all her mischief,” roars the hastily recalled General Lovegood as the Navy’s newest Admiral quietly mops the floor beside him. “We need to demand that wretched little monster be extradited here — to the country harmed by her shenanigans — to face punishment. A suitably punitive sentence should set the little villain straight!”

title: Put the Phone Down on Cold Calling?
text: A growing group of Vanilla Llama’s citizens are battling for an end to unrequested solicitations from salesmen.
chosen_option_text: “This has to stop,” says mild-mannered parent Heather Rifkin. “My family can’t even have dinner without being interrupted at least five times by telemarketers or door-to-door salesmen! My privacy is being invaded! The government ought to ban all forms of unrequested solicitations from salespeople. The sanity of the populace is at stake here!”

title: Stakes on a Plane
text: With global travel soaring, the country’s primary airport, Vanilla Llama City International, has reached full capacity. Interested parties are queuing up to share their thoughts on what should be done.
chosen_option_text: “There’s no need to destroy people’s lives just for a new runway,” parries Minerva Mason, Under-Secretary of State for Creative Solutions, “but nor do we need to turn planes away. Why not build an entirely new airport, in the Orilenyo Flow estuary? The planes can fly over the sea, and a bullet train can take passengers to the city centre. Everyone wins - well except for the local wildlife, but what’s an emu to you or me?”

title: Wipe Out Graffiti?
text: Citizens all over Vanilla Llama have been petitioning for firmer action on public graffiti.
chosen_option_text: “I don’t see what’s so bad,” comments Bella Dawson, a famous art critic. “This is urban art at its finest. It’s vibrant, colorful, and simply reeks of culture! Just look at the form displayed in this string of racist expletives! Wonderful. Simply wonderful. I think we should really be encouraging these budding Rembrandts, not putting them down! I say we legalise it, in the name of culture!”

title: Not Mushroom for Error
text: Wild mushroom season is upon Vanilla Llama again, and as is traditional, Vanilla Llamen from all over the country will go out to gather nature’s bounty. In recent years, however, there have been more and more deaths due to people mistaking poisonous fungi for harmless ones.
chosen_option_text: “Quality is the problem,” suggests Clara Cantharellus, one of Vanilla Llama’s leading mycologists. “First, let’s ban wild mushroom foraging. But also, we must increase funding for mushroom farming research. I know we can develop domesticated mushroom varieties and farming methods that would match wild ones for variation in type, good taste, and other desired properties. People can have their mushrooms and eat them without risking death too!”

title: Known Unknowns
text: In the aftermath of a series of high-profile, violent crimes, Vanilla Llama is reeling at the revelation that the identities and plans of the perpetrators had already been discovered well in advance of their crimes. However, the clever analysts who made this discovery work for the Security Intelligence Service of Brancaland, a nation historically allied to yours, who seem quite open on the fact that they’re spying on your citizens.
chosen_option_text: “This goes against the spirit of our laws,” sputters your Minister for Transparency, trying to cover the agent’s eyes. “The purpose of privacy laws is to keep the government from knowing about the private lives of citizens in any way. Don’t try to get around them through foreign loopholes. This silly objective of pre-preventing crimes is not worth it. Do we want to live in a world where the government buys blackmail information about us from foreigners?”

title: Violent Violetists Demand Blood!
text: Members of weird religious cult the Order of Violet are asking for the government to appease their mighty deity by offering Her a sacrifice of the human variety.
chosen_option_text: “Who’s being a lunatic?” retorts Georgina Kilkenny of the Vanilla Llama Humanitarian Society. “I agree that these practices ought to be outlawed, but instead of sinking to the same level of these fanatics and killing our fellow people, why not simply start a re-education program? Even the worst person can be rehabilitated into a useful member of society, with enough time, care, and lots and lots of funding!”

title: Traffic Cops Needed on Information Superhighway?
text: Certain shadowy ministerial figures have proposed government monitoring of individual internet usage.
chosen_option_text: Privacy activist Leilani Stephenson is outraged, as usual. “Tyranny is the natural result of limiting information! Someone, somewhere, will always find something offensive — mimes for example. Those scare the hell out of me. But should we ban them? No! Free the internet! We have nothing to fear from free information but pop-up advertising!”

title: Blazing Through the Paper Trail
text: Following a recent fire in the National Archive, which destroyed thousands of important documents, several vocal representatives have approached you with solutions.
chosen_option_text: “Now, hold on a second. What about us?” asks Pachacuti Strange, the CEO of a national paper supplier. “We might not have the flash of an electronic system, but I’ll tell you what we do have: quality customer service. You’re saying fires are bad. Well, we hear you loud and clear. Stick with us and not only will we make physical copies of all the files to store in different locales, but I’ll get my research team to whip up some fire-resistant paper too. Let’s see those IT poindexters do all that!”

title: Shine On, You Crazy Diamond
text: What was supposed to be a celebratory occasion — the addition of a flawless (and enormous) new diamond to the Vanilla Llaman National Museum — has instead turned into a national embarrassment. Independent experts have released a statement declaring the stone to be lab-created, casting doubt on whether the valuable display should be considered a ‘real’ gemstone.
chosen_option_text: “This isn’t my fault!” trembles gem curator Sloane Cheyney, responsible for approving the enormously expensive purchase. “The dealer assured us it was a real diamond! An opportunity like that only comes around once in a blue moon, so we had to jump on it! There needs to be a law about this; imitation wares must be clearly labeled as knock-offs, going so far as to arrest dishonest sellers!”

title: Put a Fence Around the Commons Floor?
text: Protesting a recent policy decision you made, one of your prominent cabinet ministers, Judas Benedict, today crossed the floor and joined the main opposition party. You and some more loyal ministers are now holding an emergency debate on this.
chosen_option_text: “I have a solution that renders the whole problem of floor-crossing moot,” interjects independent politician Iris Douglas from the back of the crowded room, hoping you’ll notice her. “Why don’t we simply scrap all political parties and have every politician run as an independent? Think about it! Partisan loyalty is a barrier to true freedom. Let politicians campaign on their individual merits, and represent no-one but themselves.”

title: The Devil’s Spawn
text: Big baby news from Blackacre: Supreme Leader Valeria Drake — the oft-hostile tyrant of that oft-hostile nation — has announced that she is once again pregnant. With heartfelt and sometimes sincere congratulations pouring in from leaders all across the world, eyes are turning on Vanilla Llama, eager to gauge your reaction.
chosen_option_text: A civil servant walks in on the meeting, and ruins the ambience by turning on the fluorescent ceiling lights. “Oh, uhm, s-sorry... but I came in to tell you that you could also simply ignore the entire affair. Pretend that you didn’t hear about the pregnancy because you were too busy volunteering in orphanages to follow international gossip. It’ll create a positive image of yourself, and you’ll have a great excuse to change the subject to how awesome you are.”

title: The End Is in Sight?
text: The high-profile manhunt, capture, trial and conviction of Amelia ‘Cannibal’ Hadfield has been occupying news headlines for months, and now the serial slaughterer is finally scheduled to be executed. While most executions tend to have a few people in the viewing gallery, the notoriety of the infamous ingester of infants has demand for ringside seats at an all-time high.
chosen_option_text: “The death penalty is a regrettable necessity, not an entertainment event,” intones Judicial Review Officer Vera Clinton, glaring sternly at you over her gold-rimmed spectacles. “The public should be excluded from the process of judicial execution. The convicted soul, an executioner and a single medical witness - there’s no need for anyone else in the room.”

title: Gimme Shelter
text: Recently, a transgender woman was murdered by her abusive partner, despite seeking refuge in a shelter for victims of domestic and sexual abuse days beforehand. It turns out that she was initially given shelter, but then forced to leave again when it transpired that she was transgender.
chosen_option_text: “Don’t listen to that TERF! It’s disgusting and disgraceful that anyone could try to justify a woman being sent back into such a violent and dangerous situation!” exclaims prominent transgender rights campaigner Maria Cole, threatening the author with a lacrosse stick to emphasise her point. “All women deserve protection and safety from abuse, whether they are transgender or cisgender. Women’s shelters must not discriminate! If you are a woman and you need shelter you should be granted it.”

title: Immigrants: Do They Get the Job Done?
text: The “Make Vanilla Llama Vanilla Llaman Again” Party, whose slogan is “sending immigrants back to Bigtopia as soon as we can be bothered to find it on a map,” have been rising up in recent polls. Some of your party’s strategists have suggested dealing with this by letting immigrants vote and run in elections.
chosen_option_text: “Wait, wait, I’ve got it!” pants Erin Splinter, dubbed Flip-Flopper of the Year by The Vanilla Llama Mail. “What if we just allowed immigrants to vote, but didn’t let them run for office? That way they can feel like they’re making a difference, without actually threatening the positions of esteemed politicians like yourself, Leader. So we can all be happy.” She looks around at the other two. “...Right, guys?”

title: Vexing VAT
text: A collection of shoppers and business owners have gathered outside your office to protest over the current levels of value-added tax - the sales tax that is applied to products and services at the time of purchase - also known as VAT.
chosen_option_text: “As always, there is a third option,” muses a passer-by with a voice of confidence. “There is no doubt that this tax disproportionately affects the poor, but we also can’t deny that it helps fund programmes that the poor themselves benefit from. Might I suggest reducing VAT on basic necessities while increasing it on luxury items? The rich might not like it, but it’s high time that they paid their dues to society and their fellow citizens.”

title: Chip Off the Ol’ Bloc
text: An anonymous whistleblower leaked evidence that despite banning political parties, powerful and secret blocs of politicians have begun unofficially helping each other pass and defeat legislation, effectively rendering the ban pointless.
chosen_option_text: “I’m shocked, shocked!” sarcastically replies a former Opposition backbencher while making a tally of the MPs surrounding you. “Of course, we wouldn’t have this problem if we had political parties. What you should do is reinstate national parties, and install some sort of... oh, let’s say ‘quota’ for each one. That way, people with opposing viewpoints will be fairly represented, and no one would be more powerful than anyone else.”

title: Up the Creek
text: One of the longest rivers in Vanilla Llama is also a major shipping lane in Land of Faceplace. Bigtopia, a downstream nation, has unveiled its plans to dam this river, prohibiting any ships from travelling further upstream and beyond its waters.
chosen_option_text: “The lifeblood of my people is at stake!” cries the ambassador from an upstream landlocked country. “My country’s only access to the sea is through that river! If that damned dam gets built, cargo ships would be unable to travel to and from my nation! Bigtopia won’t listen to our pleas. What do you say we and the other upstream countries gather an army and blow those asshats out of the water?”

title: A Sticky End for Leader?
text: After the recent Syrupgate Scandal (where your niece was seen eating pancakes with a non-maple-based sweetener) relations between Brancaland and Vanilla Llama have reached an all-time low. Hoping to patch things over, a formal head of state visit has been arranged. On the itinerary is an open-top ride through their national park in a traditional moose-drawn carriage. However, security staff have expressed some concerns about this.
chosen_option_text: “According to the World Census, Brancaland is in the top 5% safest nations in the world,” reassures your Minister for Diplomacy, who is known to be quite ambitious. “You’re as safe within their borders as you are within your own front room. We should show some trust in Brancalandian security arrangements. After that, I think we could boost your international standing if you visited the front lines of war-torn Maxtopia and try to bring some healing to that broken nation.”

title: Congratulations, You Have Crabs!
text: Excited ecologists have discovered that the Mark Estuary is home to a previously undiscovered colony of horseshoe crabs. Horseshoe crab blood is a highly valued source of limulus amoebocyte lysate (LAL), an important component in the production of vaccines and other medical equipment.
chosen_option_text: “Laboratory-synthesised genetically engineered recombinant factor fulfills all the same purposes as LAL,” babbles Professor Abraham Vonel-Singh, whose pungent aroma fills the room with the scent of garlic. “Ecological protections for vulnerable crab populations are essential, and even if horseshoe crab blood is cheaper, it’s a small cost for the government to subsidise artificial reagents. Keep the estuary virginal and pristine, keep those bloodsuckers away and everyone will benefit. I stake my reputation on it!”

title: Some Assembly Required
text: After an ill-advised demonstration during a floor speech on chemical safety standards, the national legislative building is in need of extensive renovations. Leading architects, lawmakers and political scientists have arranged a meeting with you to discuss designs for the new assembly chamber.
chosen_option_text: “The Brancalandian legislature is infamous for running into gridlock,” warns senior legislator Margaret Whedon. “I surmise that a traditional semicircle would be best. Tried and true by many classical governments throughout the ages, it shall add an air of gravitas to all proceedings. With an emphasis on non-fixed seating placing parliament members of different backgrounds next to one another, you’ll find the opposition less concerned with putting up a visible fight and better focused on finding ways to get the actual work of governing done.”

title: Essentially on Strike
text: Disappointed with their current wages and working conditions, disgruntled law enforcement officers have voted for strike action, leaving no one to maintain order. A majority of police officers are now refusing to work until their demands are met, in turn stirring public debate over the ethics of striking by so-called essential workers.
chosen_option_text: “Everyone has a right to strike, but everyone also has a right to essential services,” asserts idealistic student and socialist Rochelle Rios. “You just have to make sure that there’s sufficient funding and training for redundancy to exist within the system, so that essential services can cover for each other at times of industrial action. If ambulance crews are on strike, use fire patrol vehicles and police convoys. If the firefighters are on strike, then deploy the army. If the army goes on strike... well, yeah, that’s a toughie. But you get the idea.”

title: The Plane Truth
text: You’ve just returned from a pleasant “diplomatic summit” on the tropical island nation of East Calypso. As your plane approaches Vanilla Llama City Airport, bright sunlight glimmers upon the foreign names and insignia on a variety of parked aircraft. Eventually, you see a few shabby tail fins with the Air Vanilla Llama logo. The woeful assortment of filthy fuselages and peeling paint barely looks airworthy. Is the national airline truly that pathetic?
chosen_option_text: While waiting for the airplane to reach the gate, you receive a call from Bryan Ringham, a management consultant and frequent flier. He doesn’t waste time with chitchat. “Did you know that overhead at Air Vanilla Llama has seen a 380% increase over the last ten years? They won’t be competitive with numbers like that. You could help them by eliminating all regulations that prevent airlines from charging for extra services such as seat reservations, checked bags, and clean drinking water. We can have a nice, lucrative budget airline here — and maybe even create some revenue for the shareholders!”

title: You Just Sank My Battleship!
text: Last month the Vanilla Llaman Navy’s flagship scandalously sank while docked in the Lahabana Harbor. After analysis, experts concluded the primary cause was rust from poor maintenance.
chosen_option_text: “You’re all ignoring the bigger problem!” shouts a protester outside your office window, desperately trying to catch your attention, “That sunken battleship is polluting the environment horribly. All kinds of chemicals are seeping from the wreckage, and we’re doing nothing to clean it up. Instead of building yet another war machine, how about we clean up some of our old messes, starting with this shipwreck.”

title: Keep Me Appraised?
text: Your morning cabinet meeting was derailed by an impromptu rant by your Minister of Culture and Snobbery, lamenting over an art sale that did not go as planned.
chosen_option_text: “Oh please, who the hell wants more government?” spits a disgruntled cleaner, piping up from the corner of the room. “Just ban appraisals completely, and people can sell things at market levels without stupid pieces of paper or so-called educated opinions getting in the way.”

title: Time to Put the Older Senators Out to Pasture?
text: Many people are starting to think that it’s time to put term limits on elected officials, given the average age of 70 years old and 40 years of service in the nation’s Parliament.
chosen_option_text: “Wait a minute,” says Sophie Ho, chairperson of the national Infinite Power party. “We pay a lot of money to get those people into office. It can take several terms before we get a return on our investment, I mean, candidates. We should extend the number of years for each term, not limit the number of times a person can serve in any specific office!”

title: Transgender Recognition Demanded
text: After tabloid magazine “The Bun” outed supermodel Gillian Mansbridge as having been born male, the fashion world has gone into a frenzy, with the organisers of Vanilla Llama City Fashion Week barring the model from the runway. Social media has gone into meltdown with commentators from all sides of the argument demanding that the government step in.
chosen_option_text: “I have gone through twenty years of internal pain about my external appearance, and I’ve put so much effort and money into finally having the world see the real me!” blogs the model. “Gender isn’t a binary proposition: gender identity is not necessarily the gender assigned at birth. I was fortunate to have private funds and supportive parents, but not all are so lucky. Please recognise my right to self-determination of identity, and help those like me get the surgery and medicine they need.”

title: Economic Collapse Looms!
text: Big business, fed up with over-regulation in Vanilla Llama, are heading offshore in ever-increasing numbers.
chosen_option_text: “This is a catastrophe waiting to happen,” says the Chamber of Commerce. “Think of the consequences! Without big business, where do the jobs come from? Where do we get our medicine? Our cars? Our latest fashions? There are dozens of useless regulations the government could abolish today to make life easier for commerce, and it’s high time they did.”

title: We’re Dying for Your Business
text: A recent exposé of the death care industry revealed that funeral costs are leaving some families dead broke. The reason for the price increases is thought to be because while population growth continues to rise, funeral parlour growth has stopped cold, resulting in shocking cases of price gouging. Demand for last rites has become so high that families sometimes have to pawn all of the deceased’s possessions just to afford a simple burial.
chosen_option_text: “Yes, and do you know why there’s a shortage of funeral services, hmmm?” quietly seethes funeral director Igor Fronkensteen, while dragging a lumpy burlap sack behind him. “Burial plot land costs...they are rising, yes? The price of insuring a hearse these days is, how do you say, absolutely ludicrous, yes? And the restrictive laws on ‘adequate refrigeration’ and ‘treating the dead with dignity’ all are running our margins and my salary down! You want more funeral services at a cheaper price, you should ease up on the bureaucracy, yes?”

title: Being Honest
text: A politician is attempting to have his name legally changed from Harry Butts to Honest Joe Johnson so it will look more appealing on the ballot, but his opponents are crying foul.
chosen_option_text: “Hey, what if we took this a step further?” says Gretel Deming, one of your party’s more creative campaign strategists and successful parliamentarians. “As we’re listing names on the ballot, why don’t we have all our party’s candidates change their middle names just before the election to emphasise our key policies. We can use that space like a miniature campaign poster. Like my name, for example, would be Gretel ‘We Will Endure’ Deming. How could people resist voting for that?”

title: Where in the Woods Is Cindy SanFrancisco?
text: After their daughter wandered off into the woods behind her house, a pair of teary-eyed parents interrupts one of your meetings, beseeching you to step up the rescue effort.
chosen_option_text: “Yer all missin’ the heart o’ the matter,” barks Ace Kasher, a burly, crosscut-saw wielding lumberjack. “The problem isn’t these lil’ rascals gettin’ lost; it’s what they’re gettin’ lost in. If we chop down those damned woods, well then there won’t be anythin’ to get lost in, now will there? You give me and my team the OK, and we’ll make those wooded deathtraps a thing o’ the past!”

title: Licence to Breed?
text: Increasing reports of child abuse and neglect in Vanilla Llama has prompted local pressure groups to call for ‘parental licences’.
chosen_option_text: “The answer to this problem is patently obvious,” says Amelia Garcia, your Minister of Social Welfare. “The government simply needs to give more funding to the welfare department so that we can recruit more social workers to carry out regular checks on parents and judge whether or not they’re doing a good job of looking after their children. It’ll be expensive, but at least it’s a damn sight fairer than licensing parents.”

title: The Forbidden Fruit
text: The Prime Minister of the massive agricultural nation of Ausblic has sent you a rather unconventional gift: five thousand fruit baskets worth 100 marks each. Now, crates of fruit baskets occupy almost all available space in your office.
chosen_option_text: “What you call bribes, I call political donations,” divulges politician Elizabeth James, who hefts a suitcase that is bursting with cash. “Getting into public office takes millions of marks, and the average citizen cannot afford to do so. If you make it easier for politicians to receive donations from generous benefactors, you could bring equality to politics and give even the most disadvantaged candidates a fighting chance, regardless of their financial standing.”

title: A “Friend” in Need
text: The aggressive nation of Blackacre has been struck with a series of massive natural disasters that have killed tens of thousands and destroyed sanitation, transit, and economic infrastructure, with the likely consequence of great suffering for millions in the coming months. This has presented you with the moral quandary of whether or not you should come to the aid of a nation that has frequently declared its hatred for Vanilla Llama and the Vanilla Llaman way of life.
chosen_option_text: “Not that I don’t agree with Mr. Compassionate over here, but that particular method only seems to stir up unwanted trouble,” notes Ginny Scott, Vanilla Llama’s top chess master and military strategist. “Frankly, there’s a much better way of making our point without causing so much international outcry. Why not provide them aid, but so much of it that they become dependent on us for survival? Flood them with food, but do nothing to help their farmers. Supply them with power, but don’t build power infrastructure. Then, when they’ve lost any capacity to support themselves, start charging them! We can look good internationally while secretly waging war against their economy.”

title: Bullet Time
text: Regular traffic congestion within Vanilla Llama’s interstate highways has resulted in a flurry of petitions being sent to you demanding the development of a Maglev bullet train connecting the nation’s major cities. Apparently there was going to be a demonstration outside your front door as well, but the protesters got stuck in traffic.
chosen_option_text: “That angry fellow is correct, you know...” says Kelly Johnson, an agreeable businesswoman who gently guides the furious commuter to the back door, “but who is to say the burden of the cost should be on the government’s back? Me and my colleagues in Budget Rail Incorporated can get Vanilla Llama high speed connections with no cost to your taxpayers. We’ve got suppliers of nearly-new metal, fairly decent quality second-hand trains, engines that almost passed emission standards. We’ve even identified which arable land owners you’ll need to force to sell to us to make this service fast and profitable. Just sign, quickly, here, here, here, and umm... initials here...”

title: Preach With Me if You Want to Live
text: The military has seen a sharp rise in complaints against chaplains who often pressure soldiers, particularly atheists and those adhering to foreign religions, into converting prior to battle. Military officials and soldiers have come for your guidance as the chaplain issue has brought troop morale to an all time low.
chosen_option_text: “Well, the problem isn’t the presence of religion, it’s that my troops are hearing it in the wrong place,” suggests the devout seventh battalion commander, Captain Kathleen Alvarez. “We must make the military accommodating to all beliefs in the interest of tolerance and fairness. Sure, you might end up with some oddballs, like that captain in ninth battalion who worships the flying purple meatball monster or people who don’t believe anything at all, but hey, at least our troops can find their own path to spiritual enlightenment.”

title: Border Burden
text: The border between Bigtopia and Vanilla Llama has long been a messy one, with several so-called ‘pene-exclaves’ — Vanilla Llaman lands that can only be effectively accessed by passing through Bigtopia’s territory, and vice-versa. This challenge, brought on by the mountainous terrain, has been brought to the fore by an unexpected letter from Bigtopia’s ambassador.
chosen_option_text: “Are you insane? Think about our citizens!” cries Clement Quinn, your Minister of Foreign Affairs, who passed through three border checkpoints on the way to work today. “Theyd have to give up their ancestral land in order to stay with us, or else suddenly wake up in a different country! Why dont we just sign a mutual free border agreement with Bigtopia? If you live in an exclave, you’ll be able to travel without a visa to and from the mainland, and services such as the fire and police departments would be allowed to cross the border too. I’m sure we can trust that their citizens won’t exploit this to gain access to other parts of Vanilla Llama.” He shakes the hand of the Bigtopian messenger, and quietly dismisses them.

title: Lion Dad Sparks Child-Rearing Sentiment
text: The controversial book “Battle Hymn of the Lion Dad”, which depicts a foreign-born father brutally raising his children to outperform their peers, has whipped up a great debate over parenting in Vanilla Llama.
chosen_option_text: “It’s not my fault,” yawns exhausted warehouse operative and father of four Obinze Fowler, after returning from a double shift. “All I ever learned at school was how to calculate a hypotenuse and how an oxbow lake is formed. Why not teach young Vanilla Llamen some useful life skills like raising kids, getting a job, and coping with the daily grind of life? It’s all they have to look forward to, after all.” He immediately falls asleep on the couch.

title: Hackable Elections?
text: A damning new report has shown extremely strong evidence that many voting machines were hacked by operatives from Blackacre during the last election, with votes for the opposition parties being counted as votes for your party. Furious opposition members and ethics watchdogs have demanded that you take action.
chosen_option_text: “Um, are we forgetting about the MASSIVE VOTER FRAUD that took place here?” fumes the Opposition Leader, thrusting the report in your face. “The previous election must be declared null and void, and any laws passed since then must be stricken. A new election needs to be declared immediately, and international corruption watchdogs must oversee the whole ordeal. This government is tainted with corruption, and we owe it to the people of Vanilla Llama to present them with fair and democratic elections.”

title: Cui Bono?
text: Conservative media news source Brightheart’s recent exposé claiming that 25% of domestic terrorist funding comes from welfare fraud has sparked an earnest debate across Vanilla Llama on welfare reform.
chosen_option_text: “I say unto you that the answer is more welfare, not less!” offers unemployed youth Khalida Violetsglory, pushing a shopping trolley of ammonium nitrate and diesel oil to the checkout till. “If you increase welfare, then maybe the resentful disenfranchised minorities will feel more supported by society, and become less prone to radicalisation. What have you got to lose?”

title: Big Brother Is Watching You Surf
text: Advisers from Vanilla Llama’s security services have created a small piece of spyware that they would like to install on every computer in the nation so they can track activity.
chosen_option_text: “While ‘tis not my place,” says Amish farmer Jamal Gaudí, “I just thought I’d mention that we Amish don’t have any of this so-called ‘cyber-crime’. Aye, ‘tis a boring life, and plowin’ gets old, but abolishing all of those computer-machines would certainly solve thy problems. Perhaps ye should just abandon phones and fax machines, too. Then ye’ll be on your way to livin’ in an Amish paradise!”

title: “Don’t Dam Our Rivers, Damnit!” Say Protesters
text: A group of Greenpeace protesters have called for an end to a government proposal to begin damming rivers in Vanilla Llama to increase water supplies and generate power.
chosen_option_text: “Think before you open your mouth,” says engineer Reginald Gibson. “While Vanilla Llama may have to pay the price in animal diversity, as well as adverse effects on the environment, do we really want fossil-fuel based plants polluting Vanilla Llama? If you use your common sense, I think you’ll find that damming some rivers would be a good idea. Plus, think of how much the economy would benefit from all the jobs these projects would create.”

title: Your Assignment, Should You Choose to Accept It
text: A coalition of middle-schoolers and educators have come into the spotlight for proposing that homework should be banned, claiming that it disadvantages the poor.
chosen_option_text: “There is a legitimate concern raised here,” says Homer, an annoyingly hipster teacher, who prefers that his students address him by his first name only. “I agree homework should be banned for the sake of the poorer students, but it is a good source of cognitive production. Therefore, I propose a compromise: let’s ban homework, but even it out by lengthening the school day.”

title: Outed Teacher Ousted
text: A religious high school in Vanilla Llama City has caused quite a stir after firing a teacher because of his homosexual orientation.
chosen_option_text: “This is yet another example of what harm religion does to our society,” says LGBTQ activist Leandro Clinton, waving a rainbow flag. “Homosexuality shouldn’t be a taboo subject anymore. Children ought to be brought up knowing that sexual diversity is just something that exists in society and is completely normal. To help society move forward, we need to get rid of religious schooling and teach that people should love whoever and whatever they want.”

title: For Crying Out Loud
text: A large portion of Emu City was recently consumed by a raging fire. A newly-published report investigating the unprecedented scale of the disaster revealed that the town crier was home sick, which made it impossible for the town’s citizens to coordinate an emergency response.
chosen_option_text: A strange man who introduces himself as Doctor Howe bursts into your office. “You must have telephone booths on the streets! It’s a matter of life and death! If you’re worried about people using them frivolously for gossip, we can always set them up so they only connect to emergency services. That way you can have the instant response of phones without all the hassle of people talking on them all the time.”

title: A Lack of Comma Sense
text: After your highest-ranking legislative aide dedicated his new memoir to ‘my parents, Leader and Maxx’, unreputable news sources, the Emu Gazette and the Vanilla Llama Times have been harassing your office incessantly about nepotism in your administration. An assortment of advisers have met with you over some bamboo soup to discuss this serial issue.
chosen_option_text: “The serial comma can just as easily add ambiguous meaning, and just takes up space unnecessarily,” replies photographer Falala Fox as she tries to shoot the leaves before she eats. “Don’t you find its usage to be not correct? And are you ready to convince the taxpayer of the extra expense they will be taking on? Because that’s what you will have to do.”

title: The Body Politic
text: Ubalin, a small city in southwestern Vanilla Llama, was formerly a monarchical city-state before being annexed in the early history of Vanilla Llama. DNA testing on the remains of the last king of Ubalin, King Oswyn V, traced his lineage to a local man in a poor district of Vanilla Llama City.
chosen_option_text: “Maybe there’s a compromise,” speculates Efthamia Kwan, a prolific jouster and part-time turnip farmer. “How about instead of making him the absolute monarch of Ubalin, we install King... Rex as a constitutional monarch of Ubalin. That way Ubalin stays a part of Vanilla Llama and continues to be run by competent politicians, but they’ll have a bit of tradition to rally behind. And imagine having an actual king open the Ubalin medieval fayre. My turnip sales will go through the roof!”

title: Bombshell for Leader
text: Your re-election campaign has been thrust into the headlines due to adult film star Catherine Gratwick announcing her full-throated support. She has since hooked up with your campaign manager to offer her services on the campaign trail.
chosen_option_text: “Screw her!” shouts your self-appointed morals counselor, Prue Dish, confiscating your brother’s movies while he is busy cheering. “Gratwick is a disgusting, disgraceful deviant! Those are the triple Ds of her profession. You can’t possibly get into bed with people like her! Listen to Prudence: denounce her. Reassure the public that you’ve never even heard of those demeaning films — you haven’t, have you — and send demure surrogates to represent you. That prim actress who’s been in the soap Hard Days on Easy Street for fifty years just loves you.”

title: We Can’t Cross That Bridge When We Come to It
text: Several workers were killed and others injured in the recent collapse of a bridge being constructed across the Emu River.
chosen_option_text: “Objection!” cries prominent attorney Carter Ross, representing construction firm Bricks An’ Stuff. “These destructive laws would merely hinder businesses’ ability to perform their job: providing houses to our beautiful citizens, storefronts to our busy workers, and hotel skyscrapers to our guests!” He pats down his suit before handing you a trunk filled with legislation suggestions. “Offer subsidies to businesses that perform safety checks, and trust companies to carry them out. They know what’s best, after all.”

title: Many Are Called
text: Yesterday, the judiciary released a study showing that nearly half of all people called for jury service are excused, with most citing childcare or medical issues as the reason. You’ve walked down the street from your office to Vanilla Llama City courthouse to investigate more yourself.
chosen_option_text: “The reason why people don’t want to go to jury service is because time is literally money,” observes an idiot who doesn’t know what ‘literally’ means. “You should pay people for their jury time at an amount equal to earnings lost. For care commitments, pay for help. For medical problems, bring medical support into the courtroom. Any problem can be surmounted if you’re willing to pay to solve it.”

title: Throwing Paleontologists a Bone
