text: After a commercial fossil hunter discovered an incredibly rare and nearly complete Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton, and subsequently announced their intent to sell it to the highest bidder at an auction house, a debate kicked off on the ethics of for-profit fossil hunting. One of your more dinosaur-obsessed aides has convinced you to visit a dig site and obtain first-hand knowledge on the matter.
chosen_option_text: “These bones are a limited-time offer,” states Tracy Matei, the fossil hunter at the center of the controversy, slinging a jackhammer behind her back. “The government will never have the funding to find and collect them all, so they’d probably be eroded away in a few years anyway. Besides, fossil hunting is a great hobby; it gets people outdoors, educates them about Vanilla Llama’s past, and can even put some cash in their pockets if they’re lucky. Just disseminate some basic guidelines on documentation so citizens can help preserve the scientific record, and encourage the free market to compete.”

title: Zinc Before You Mint
text: After massive cost cutting, composition changes, and selling the break room foosball table, the Vanilla Llaman Mint has reduced the production cost of their smallest denomination coin to equal its face value. However, after the coins entered circulation, it was found that changing the primary metal from copper to zinc has made them toxic if ingested. After countless incidents of zinc poisoning in children and pets, many are questioning the government’s miserly attitude to safety.
chosen_option_text: “Now, now, hold on a second,” chimes in Mint Director Ash Rubio, pulling coins stuck between the couch cushions. “We can’t just take millions of coins out of circulation — that would simply be a logistical nightmare and a colossal waste of the taxpayer’s money! Instead, perhaps we simply just instruct children to avoid putting any foreign objects in their mouth, like these coins we’re quibbling about. Those kids, they watch those silly cartoons, right? Why, if we put the PSAs in there, they won’t even notice they’re being taught.”

title: Life in the Bike Lane
text: Tragedy struck Vanilla Llama City when a cyclist was killed by a transport truck, making this the thirteenth such incident in the past few weeks. This has propelled activists to peddle the idea of creating additional bike lanes in Vanilla Llama’s cities.
chosen_option_text: “What do we want? Bike lanes! When do we want them? Now!” chants cyclist Anthony Schmidt, five-time winner of the Tour de Vanilla Llama competition. “Many of us in the big cities rely on our bikes to go about our daily business. If anything, more cyclists on the streets will mean fewer cars, and that means less congestion. Less congestion means less pollution, and that makes everyone healthier in the long run. It may be more inconvenient for the motorists, but if they don’t like it, they can go honk themselves.”

title: Arms Industry Demands Respect
text: Representatives of Vanilla Llama’s arms manufacturing industry have expressed outrage over the lack of public and private support for their sector.
chosen_option_text: Your Minister of Trade advises taking a middle ground: “We can’t ban arms sales without harming the quality of our military and police departments, not to mention the economy. These hippies do have a point though - guns are terrible things in the wrong hands. We should implement additional safety checks on the groups to which the weapons get sold. That way we don’t lose too many sales, and the people are persuaded we are making a stand against nations who use the weapons for immoral ends. The arms industry get to sell their guns and the protesters get to protest. Everybody wins!”

title: Malpractice Makes Perfect
text: The notorious Dr. Gerhard Dwelling, a medical diagnostician famed for his unorthodox but impeccably successful approach to medicine, has been described with words such as “genius” and “nutjob”, but most recently “unemployed”. Dwelling was fired for malpractice after he gave one of his patients a supposedly lethal cocktail of drugs. Once he had packed his belongings, it was found that his patient had made a miraculous recovery.
chosen_option_text: “My confidence in myself far outweighs that of these regulations supposedly designed to ‘protect’ people,” states Dr. Dwelling after ingesting some white pills from an unmarked bottle. “If I had played by the rules that patient would be six feet under, but they fired me anyway. The bureaucrats that run hospitals aren’t the ones treating patients, all they care about is covering their proverbial behinds. Perhaps they wouldn’t need to if Vanilla Llama had a little faith in their medical professionals, and let us take whatever risks we need to in bad situations. There may be mishaps, but I can guarantee that there will be more lives saved than lost.” He picks up his cane and promptly hobbles out of your office.

title: Is Our Children Learning?
text: When a relatively minor official in your government vowed to increase the standard of education in Vanilla Llama, the press came knocking on your door to ask how this might actually be done.
chosen_option_text: “As we’ve proven in the past, the free market can manage this far better than the public sector,” says market-analyst Percy Patel. “Now, I’m not saying that the state shouldn’t help people go to school - far from it. Still, schools need greater freedom to maximize learnedness: to set their own tuition, salaries, curricula, etc. Give private schools a small government subsidy, and let the free market take its course. So what if a few poor kids drop out earlier? You can’t make omelettes without breaking a few eggs.”

title: Trouble in Deed
text: During a photo op in a fairly upscale neighborhood of Vanilla Llama City, you notice a surprising number of abandoned houses dotting nearly every street. According to the painfully grinning woman whose baby you’re kissing, the properties are still owned by Vanilla Llaman expats who emigrated to various other countries, often decades ago.
chosen_option_text: “You can’t do that!” screeches your rarely seen Minister of Sanity, crawling out of the woodwork of a nearby house. “Imagine what would happen if we let some mayor seize property just because it isn’t being used, especially if that property is owned by expats who might have dual citizenship! Do you want an international incident on our hands? The government needs to do things by the book, and not stir up any trouble. Instead, let’s try to contact every person that owns unused property here, and ask if they’d be willing to sell.”

title: Rodents of Unusual Sociability
text: Your brother’s pet guinea pig has been looking a little down recently, and a pet psychiatrist has revealed that this is a consequence of loneliness.
chosen_option_text: “If a guinea pig is too miserable, its owner can just dispose of it and get a happier-looking one,” suggests passer-by Lola Bale, tossing a pet cat into a nearby wheeled bin. “Darwinism will take care of the rest, and within a few generations you’ll have a selected population of guinea pigs that doesn’t mind being alone.”

title: Vanilla Llama Is Never Ever Getting Back Together... Like Ever
text: After a printing error on the official Vanilla Llaman map left off the tiny Emu Peninsula, its sole inhabitant, Mike Ronation, declared independence from Vanilla Llama. Following his arrest of a mailman who failed to enter the “proper customs”, a group of concerned citizens have asked you to address the threat posed by Mr. Ronation. His protest has already spawned several secessionist movements almost overnight.
chosen_option_text: “Making him needlessly suffer seems a tad bit extreme,” suggests Mike’s concerned grandmother Hayley Moriarty. “Sure, I’m a little upset that Mike doesn’t want to be part of our wonderful country and that he tried to snap that mailman’s neck, but you have to look at it from both perspectives. If the government wants to win back Mike and the secessionists he instigated, they could start by allowing greater autonomy to regions that want it. I’m sure that Mikey will gladly return to us if you show a little love and understanding.”

title: Rivers of Blood
text: Dye effluent from a textile factory has turned the waters of a neighboring river a vivid red, angering nearby residents. The incident has placed the practices of the dye industry and the use of synthetic dyes squarely in the limelight.
chosen_option_text: “Lavender lagoons? Scarlet streams? Count me in!” chimes tourism and novelty museum tycoon Gillian Cage. “Finding chemicals in the water is anything but a problem; in fact, it’s a prime opportunity! We should add a bit of color to our lackluster lakes; the oddly-pigmented oddities would become tourist magnets! Our nation will be known far and wide for its colorful waterways, flowing proudly in our national hues. This, right here, is what will attract more money than anything Vanilla Llama has seen in ages. Let’s dye ourselves into the next golden age!”

title: Great Balls of Fire!
text: Vanilla Llama is abuzz with news of a huge meteorite - dubbed ‘Big Max’ by the media - which smashed into a large town on the outskirts of Vanilla Llama City yesterday, killing thousands and leaving behind nothing but a smouldering crater.
chosen_option_text: “That’s all well and good,” interjects Professor Charles Disney, leading scientist at the Vanilla Llama Meteorological Office. “Except that the chances of a fall of this magnitude occurring twice in the same area are miniscule at worst. I propose you direct your funding to the real issue here - rebuilding the homes and properties that have been lost, and tending to the injured and traumatised. As soon as we’ve removed what’s left of Big Max for studying, you can make a start.”

title: A Matter of Trust
text: A new survey conducted by private organizations has found out that confidence in Vanilla Llama’s political system is at an all-time low. Politicians and political think tanks are scrambling to find a solution.
chosen_option_text: “It’s probably because we’re constantly seeing the same people in power over and over again,” argues Sue-Ann Deming, a columnist for the Vanilla Llama Inquirer. “We should shake things up a bit and bring some fresh faces into the political game. Let’s introduce term limits on all public offices. That’ll definitely increase confidence in our political system!”

title: Suits in Protest
text: Thousands of business men and women have taken to the streets in protest of their working conditions and pay. “It’s not fair that we can’t have a union,” says Desmond Nguyen, VP of Sales at SlothCorp. “Just because we make six figures doesn’t mean we don’t deserve overtime too! It’s high time that the lower classes come to appreciate our hard efforts.”
chosen_option_text: Noddy Claus, secretary of labor, advises you to adjust laws to allow white-collar unions. “It only makes sense that all of the workers in our nation have an equal opportunity to benefit from the advantages of collective bargaining.”

title: Sheepish Students
text: A school in the tiny village of Piddleton, that lies in a sparsely populated and mountainous district of Vanilla Llama, has just enrolled twenty-four sheep from a nearby farm as students. The inability to fill the student number quotas mandated by the Local Authority — that help to keep schools financially viable — would have otherwise meant the closure of the school.
chosen_option_text: “What other choice did I have?” bemoans School Headteacher Clara Mendez, as she points out the village of Piddleton on a map to alleviate everyone’s curiosity. “This is the only school in Piddleton and it has served our community well for generations — the next nearest school is a two hour commute away. In a village of our size, these quotas are impossible to fill. You cannot allow local governments to impose these restrictions on any school, especially in rural districts.”

title: Anything You Can Do, I Can Do Better
text: Yesterday evening, talk radio pundit Elena Cheswick launched a scathing critique of your “ridiculously incompetent Transport Minister” and the minister’s “terrible mismanagement of timetables”. Unfortunately, said minister angrily phoned in to argue her case, and foolishly told the talkshow host that if she thought she could do better, she’d be welcome to try. Somewhat predictably, Cheswick is now outside the parliament building, ready to give it a go.
chosen_option_text: “Look at her strutting about, that know-it-all, trying to tell the public how my damn job should be done,” snarls your extremely experienced Transport Minister. “What the hell does she know about fuel logistics, or network maintenance, or sub-contract management? Absolutely jack nothing, that’s what! Broadcasters shouldn’t be allowed to offer unfounded opinions about things they know nothing about. Slap a fine on her for misleading the public and fomenting ignorance — that’ll teach her to mind her words.”

title: Feeling Down
text: Tragedy struck when commercial airline pilot Avinash Pavlov deliberately crashed his airplane into a mountain, causing the death of the 416 passengers and 12 crew on board. Afterwards, a medical report was leaked to the press revealing that the pilot had been declared “unfit for work” and suicidal by his doctor, but had failed to report this information to his employer.
chosen_option_text: “Look, the solution doesn’t have to involve breaches of confidentiality and invasions of privacy,” suggests a rep from the Federation Union of Commercial United Pilots. “The problem is a different one. Pilots in this country are completely mistreated, with airlines working them too hard for adequate mental health. It’s no wonder that some of them get depressed, or burn out. Airlines should be made to pay better wages, to provide more sociable hours, and to grant more paid downtime between flights.”

title: One Wife Is Never Enough, Say Polygamists
text: A small religious group is lobbying the government to allow them to take multiple wives.
chosen_option_text: “This is nothing more than sexual deviants using religion as a pretext for perversion!” says Reverend Emory Hawkins. “Marriage is one man, one woman, and death do we part. What’s so hard to get? Anything else is a perversion, and must be banned.”

title: Blinded by the Light
text: It is a Vanilla Llaman tradition to light up one’s home with demonstrative holiday lights during festive seasons. While this has always been a distractive issue for drivers, one rather competitive neighborhood in Vanilla Llama City caused quite a stir. The strobe lights and military-grade lasers used in several displays caused multiple traffic accidents and temporary blindness, prompting a national discussion on this issue and scores of lawsuits.
chosen_option_text: “Compromise, everyone!” exclaims your Minister of Compromises, who has been appearing in far too many meetings recently. “I agree that banning holiday lights is a ridiculous idea, but at the same time we can’t ignore the risks to public health and safety. So how about we mandate that the manufacturers tone down the brightness in their lights and ban the sale of military grade lasers and excessively bright strobe lights to the public? That way people still get their lights and nobody risks getting blinded! It sure beats spending the holidays in a hospital.”

title: Ambassadors Behaving Madly
text: The privilege of diplomatic immunity for ambassadors has entered the news after several of them have been caught in unsavory behavior, including drunk driving, fist fights, and the attempted murder of a Brancalandian Member of Parliament. Concerned citizens and outraged foreign nationals have asked your government to step in and bring your ambassadors in line.
chosen_option_text: “Being a diplomat is so stressful,” complains Marco Haggard, your former ambassador to Tasmania, who has taken it upon himself to stop the fighting between the two ministers. “You send us off to these dangerous hellholes all across Land of Faceplace. Is it any wonder that some of us snap? Our job is to promote the nation’s interests and help find new allies. We need diplomatic immunity to ensure our safety as national envoys, guarantee our freedom of movement, and maybe let off some steam on the weekends. I think a little international embarrassment is a small price to pay for that.”

title: One in the Oven
text: The death of three young children, who succumbed to sun stroke after being forgotten in the back seats of a poorly-ventilated vehicle, has sparked heated debate.
chosen_option_text: “According to our studies, most of these tragedies are caused by parents who are overworked and exhausted,” says your Officer of Safety Statistics, while staring at a photo of her child before nodding out for a moment and waking up with a jolt. “The government should pay for childcare support, and additional paid leave for parents of school-aged children.”

title: Knitters in a Knot Over Police Stitch Up
text: After a peaceful public knitting class was dispersed by riot police, the citizenry are up in arms at what they perceive as unnecessary police brutality.
chosen_option_text: “Retraining the entire police force would cost far too much,” your financial advisor says quietly, appearing from behind your chair. “That being said, the crazy lady with the woolly hat is right, we do have to do something about this situation. We can’t have the police force appear brutal and unruly. What we should do is universally ban all sorts of dangerous weapons. That way the police force won’t have to worry about dangerous thugs with guns, and the public can rest easy knowing the police force won’t be able to brutally attack them either. And we can get rid of the riot police too as they clearly won’t be needed, which saves us money! Everybody wins!”

title: Bottled Up Problems
text: Panic has spread across Vanilla Llama after a study found some bottled water manufactured in Vanilla Llama to be contaminated by E. coli. Consumers’ rights groups have called on you to address this problem, so you’re attending a tour of Vanilla Llama’s largest bottling plant with some interested parties.
chosen_option_text: “There’s a sensible solution to all this,” states health inspector Jadzia Khachaturian, opening a bottle of water while wearing goggles and a respirator. “Hire more health inspectors! We can take some money from some less vital government programs, like welfare and the military, and then send in government inspectors to do daily testing on the water sources and filtration systems. Also, would it kill you to raise our salaries a bit? Because E. coli in your next meal might.”

title: Raise Duel Standards, Say Fencers
text: A number of well-dressed gentlemen wearing a varied assortment of swords are insisting that they be allowed to settle their private disputes on the field of honourable battle.
chosen_option_text: “Swords? Heavens, what dreadful things. All sharp and pointy - quite dangerous, you know,” says Jazz Zahm, an ardent pacifist. “Duelling ought to be banned! The best way to settle these kind of arguments are through judicially-supervised mediation, we all know that. If we go ahead with what these duelling nutters want, then innocent people will die! It will be a sad day when people value money more than justice. Apart from lawyers, obviously.”

title: Close Encounters of the Sci-Fi Kind?
text: A recent, well-publicized UFO sighting over rural areas of Vanilla Llama has turned people’s attention to the skies, and what... or who... might be up there.
chosen_option_text: “This event proves one thing: there are other life-forms out there,” says eccentric astronomer Khalida Cage, “All we have to do is find them! What is the price of a few hundred radio telescopes compared to the benefit of living in peace and harmony with our brethren of the stars?”

title: Thora and Eloise
text: The cross-country crime-spree of two women, Thora Dobbs and Eloise Mulholland, kept the nation hooked to their TV sets for several days, and ended in tragedy with their joint suicide pact. The unfolding story has given the pair a strange anti-hero celebrity status, with many tearful and sighing fans laying flower wreaths and shell-casings around the burnt out wreck of their car. The press are awaiting a statement from your office on the matter.
chosen_option_text: “But this isn’t daubing some graffito,” says Emily Zahm, the so-called Hanging Judge of Vanilla Llama City. “These gals weren’t Robin Hood. They robbed seventeen convenience stores, shot three people, and stole clothes from my Mama’s washing line. Let’s call a spade a spade, here: they’re evil. They deserved to plunge off the Emu Viaduct.”

title: Something Is Rotten in the State of Vanilla Llama
text: Vanilla Llama has hardly changed its electoral constituencies since King Maxbari IV ruled ancient Maxtopia. After a politician was recently elected to represent 3 people and an emu, people have begun debating the merits of reforming electoral areas, and eliminating the so-called “rotten” constituencies.
chosen_option_text: “Aren’t we supposed to be a democracy?” shouts political activist Ammon Stoltenberg, who has never voted in an election due to living in a town that was an unincorporated bog the last time electoral borders were drawn. “It’s inherently unfair that a tiny burrow of inbred farmers gets as many - or even more - representatives as new and major population centres. The government must redraw the electoral map so each seat is elected by the same number of voters.”

title: Side Effects
text: Emu Pharmaceuticals, a major international drug company based in Vanilla Llama, was recently linked to illegal human experimentation and an organ harvesting cult in the underdeveloped, jungle nation of Kawandaland. Its atrocities exposed, the company has gone bottom-up, throwing Vanilla Llaman markets into turmoil, and largely eliminating access to inexpensive medical supplies in Kawandaland.
chosen_option_text: “Oh, I’d love to bandage up Kawandaland too, ambassador,” chimes in Amina Gennaro, a top-level official in the Finance Ministry. “You do realize that our economy is being wounded by this catastrophe as well, right? I agree that the situation in Kawandaland is a sad one, but we must save ourselves while we still have the chance. Instead of spending millions of marks on medical aid, we should use those funds to stabilize our markets. It might seem cold and heartless, but I’m just following triage procedures, and I believe the bleeding is worse here in Vanilla Llama.”

title: My Chemical Romance
text: A man in Vanilla Llama City suffered a widely publicized death after drinking a concoction sold to him by an esoteric medicine vendor. He had ingested the liquid — which contained lead, arsenic, and other toxic substances — because he had been told it was a love potion that would increase his charisma and help him attract his beloved.
chosen_option_text: “Woah there, it is SO not groovy that these little numbers are sendin’ people to the sky, man,” says your Minister of Peace, Love, and Bureaucracy, swirling around one of the Madame’s potions until it starts glowing bright blue. “We should, I dunno, make a Ministry of Radical Brewskis to approve potions for sale, and ensure only approved mystical healers that have been thoroughly vibe-checked by the government can administer them. By the way, I saw your niece making some bogus mud pies without written approval. Keep your fam in line, ya dig?”

title: What Wood You Do?
text: Generous reforestation subsidies have been eagerly seized by land developers, but critics are complaining that a large proportion of these new forests lack necessary biodiversity.
chosen_option_text: “You have to be able to see the wood from the trees,” counters industry fatcat Vladimir Barren-Harkonion, digging greasy fingers into an enormous bag of chips he is working his way through. “To be frank, monocultural forests are far more commercially viable, and we need those margins to encourage private sector participation. These money-hating tree huggers would rather us create no new forests than see philanthropists like me do some good! Do you want your money to go into tiny copses, or vast tracts of canopied green land? If you’ll boost up those subsidies and allow us to plant more tracts of forest, we’ll experience the best of both worlds!”

title: A Day of Prayer
text: Last month, outrage swept the nation after many of the nation’s faithful were denied time off on Saint Ymir’s Day, being required to work under threat of termination. As religious observance increases, more and more citizens are calling for official recognition of the holiday.
chosen_option_text: “He’s right, we shouldn’t force people to observe a single religion’s holiday,” ponders your Minister of Culture. “We should recognize every religious holiday. Take Throwing Bananas On Roofs Day for instance, where the followers of Yellowism spread whimsy and yellow across the land! Complete freedom, and new cultural experiences every week.”

title: Prayer in Public Schools?
text: In order to save the souls of Vanilla Llama’s children from eternal damnation, it has been suggested that a daily prayer be made mandatory in schools nationwide.
chosen_option_text: “That’s a lily-livered compromise,” says Rebecca Washington, chairperson of the Atheist Activist Association. “Religion should have no place in our schools. We should pass laws enforcing secularity on all educational establishments.”

title: A Case of Poor Turnaround
text: The Emu Room — a Vanilla Llama City nightclub known as a swinging hotspot — was recently the site of a tragic fire that started with a flaming sambuca shot and ended claiming the lives of hundreds. Fire investigators have attributed the high number of deaths to multiple causes, but most notably the large revolving door which was the only access to the premises, which panicked crowds jammed against as they tried to escape the blaze.
chosen_option_text: “Imagine being pushed from behind, trying to get through a door which you know is unlocked, but which is providing no escape because of the mass of people trying to get through,” narrates criminal legislator Melody Grove. “The simple solution? Doors that swing outwards. Every revolving door must either be flanked by or replaced by swing doors, and proper fire exits must be built into every building that is accessible to the public.”

title: War Never Changes
text: Whilst negotiating a landmark trade deal with the small yet prosperous nation of Qaanpaluk, a nation Vanilla Llama was at war with hundreds of years ago, it was discovered that no formal declaration of peace was signed in spite of the years of de facto peace.
chosen_option_text: “Hold it right there!” exclaims Tamara Maldonado, your Minister of Administrative Affairs, as she snatches the napkin from the ambassador’s hands and tucks it neatly into her breast pocket. She then heaves a dusty file box onto your desk. “Take a look at all this stuff I dug up relating to this war. We can’t just let bygones be bygones so easily; there’s so many other things we need to iron out before we can proceed with formal peace. Check out this territorial dispute over this island... which sank into the ocean. And this island... which is now claimed by Skandilund. Regardless, we must look into these things! Weeks, perhaps months of complex negotiations and the perusal of ancient documents must be carried out before we can even think about ending this war, let alone starting trade!”

title: Private Lab Holds Vanilla Llama’s Sick to Ransom
text: Scientists at a private medical research laboratory have announced that they have produced a drug which will combat Vanilla Llama’s most notorious malady - Spon Plague.
chosen_option_text: “That’s a disgraceful way to think!” says equal rights activist Fumiko Song. “So the people who need the most help shouldn’t get any? I propose that the government takes over the distribution of all drugs so everyone can benefit from them, rich or not! That way the money-hungry corporations won’t profit from the suffering of the masses. Of course there will be the matter of a small tax rise to fund it - but what’s that when lives will be saved?”

title: The Cake Is a Lie
text: In recent weeks, a neighbouring nation in Land of Faceplace released a controversial and gory movie about Vanilla Llama, entitled The Baker Of Vanilla Llama. The movie, which follows the horrifying journey of a hapless ex-baker into the criminal underworld of Vanilla Llama City, seems to imply that Vanilla Llama is a dystopian hellhole filled with violent crime. Unsurprisingly your citizenry is offended.
chosen_option_text: “Lies and videotape, eh?” muses Lenny Groovesteel, your Propaganda Minister, reading a psychology article on The Triumph Of The Will. “Two can play at that game. We should direct our own movie directors to churn out some counter-information, singing our nation’s praises and fabricating something nasty about theirs. Have you heard people talking about the disgusting Dog-Hair Muffins they bake? No? We will fix that.”

title: Shh! Spoilers!
text: After one of your recent speeches included an accidental spoiler for the bestselling novel Hexicon, angry librarians, teenagers, and fantasy aficionados have completely surrounded your office in protest. After a hard day’s work, you have agreed to meet with the protesters, if only so that you can get out of the building.
chosen_option_text: “Speeches, not spoilers!” chants your teenage niece, who has been leading the protest. “Look, I’m trying to be a good citizen here, paying attention to what’s going on around me, but if you’re going to spoil something that I haven’t even had chance to read, then I’m not going to bother! If you really need to talk about stuff that isn’t politics in your speeches, at least warn us about it! Sure, it might look a bit silly, but who cares? This is almost as bad as when I was told that Planet of the Emus was Land of Faceplace all along!”

title: Drug Legality Run Amok
text: After a nine-year-old child died of a heroin overdose yesterday, much of the public is in an uproar over the absence of drug laws in Vanilla Llama.
chosen_option_text: “Drugs by one name, sacred plants by another,” intones His High Holiness of a major religion, daubing holy oil on your forehead. “The Church has historically used extracts of consecrated substances to open the vistas of piety and bring oneself closer to the Supreme Being. With modern pharmaceutical techniques, we can easily manufacture enough to infuse the water supply of all of Vanilla Llama, just like we do with fluoride. Is spiritual transcendence a less worthy cause than cavity prevention? I think not.”

title: The Silent Majority’s Roaring Mouthpiece
text: Mike Bakker recently won your party’s primary for a crucial seat despite a never-ending slew of controversies. He’s brash, impolite and frequently resorts to schoolyard insults, but his supporters are fervent and unwavering. Your advisers worry that further association with him will cost you votes in the next election.
chosen_option_text: “The problem is the lack of vetting at the nomination process,” suggests Pedro Meyer of the party’s South Vanilla Llama Riding Association. “The allegations against him didn’t come out until after the nomination took place so our hands were tied. We need better screening of potential candidates, extensive background checks, weeding out problematic beliefs, and the ability to swap out candidates if any... undesirable nominees slip through the cracks.”

title: Exhaust Every Option
text: Three days ago smog levels in the inner city reached a record-breaking high, with visibility so poor that a driver mistook a closed-off construction zone for an off-ramp and plummeted to his death. The public has raised the question of whether automobiles are causing too much pollution.
chosen_option_text: “Legislating against polluting cars is not going to solve the problem, as car companies will always find some loophole or deception to trick the system,” observes CEO of IntraCoil Motors, Oolong Musk. “Electric vehicles don’t pollute locally, so if everyone drove them, we would have clean air in the cities. The government should fund the creation of charging stations, to give customers the choice to realistically switch to green technologies, like the new IntraCoil Model LXIX, available next month at your local dealership.” He winks at a nearby camera.

title: Westfailian Sovereignty
text: After the United Federation sent two police cars, a police helicopter, five drones and a wind-up toy into Vanilla Llama to capture “Mega Momo”, a Vanilla Llaman citizen and alleged terrorist, the government has called a special meeting to see what should be done about this blatant breach of sovereignty.
chosen_option_text: “Are you mad?” exclaims Grace Sorin, one of your more queasy ministers, while trying to conceal her worry beads. “The United Federation has Gigadeath 4000 planes, Smashtastic 2000 helicopters and Udienow 500 missiles, and we barely have glorified crop-dusters! We need to engage the international community and try to convince them to join us in enacting sanctions against the United Federation. That will show them we’re serious!”

title: Cheques and Balances
text: After the Governor of the Central Bank of Vanilla Llama stonewalled a parliamentary committee during a two-hour hearing, refusing to answer any questions about the current state of their balance sheet, an unusual coalition of left- and right-wing political activists have come together to demand a fresh approach at the CBVL.
chosen_option_text: “Is this really the state of public debate in this country?” bemoans centrist commentator Kitty Wade, wearing a Give Multilateral Diplomacy, Without Ruling Out The Possibility Of Surgical Military Action, A Chance tie-pin. “The independence of central banking is a key component of any modern economy. Compromising that will only lead to our monetary policy becoming subject to either populism or corruption, and make us the laughing stock of Land of Faceplace. You must stand firm and defend the Bank’s independence.”

title: Of Mice and Meth
text: A growing number of citizens are reporting sightings of strange animal behavior since the nation’s water supply was drugged, ranging from carelessness and daredevilry to frantic dancing.
chosen_option_text: “Whoa, who cares about, like, a few pesky rats? This water is, like, poisoning our pets, dude,” says Sophie Myers, an enthusiastic pet lover who was particularly thirsty this morning. “You don’t have to, like, stop stoning the water, but maybe you should sell some safe water specifically for pets or whatever. You could even make it taste funny to make people not wanna drink it. Then, like, maybe my bunnies won’t try to breathe water anymore.”

title: Preach It!
text: Street preachers delivering their sermons and self-proclaimed salvation have been popping up all over Vanilla Llama.
chosen_option_text: “There is a better way to go about this,” suggests Nyota Dawson, your Minister of Compromises. “The most common complaints against street preaching are on the grounds of harassment and noise pollution. I say the most logical approach is to administer permits to those who wish to speak on public property, with a police presence to make sure they don’t cause any trouble. That’s fair, right?”

title: The Violet Mile
text: With an increasing number of inmates on death row, more commonly referred to as The Violet Mile, concerned experts from all walks of life have asked you about which method of capital punishment is the best to use on Vanilla Llama’s felons.
chosen_option_text: “Maybe we should aim to be as humane as possible when we take life?” asks machine-tool specialist Wesley Burke, holding a claw hammer in each hand. “We got bolt guns that butchers used to use in the slaughterhouses, back before you put them out of work with those veggie-laws. BAM. One bolt, one kill. Fast, effective, only a little messy.” He looks down at a circle of splattered mess on the floor. “Is anyone else getting hungry talking about this?”

title: Still Life
text: After losing a lengthy legal battle with his mother-in-law, Yasuyuki Rodriguez is making a final petition to you. He is seeking permission to remove life support from his wife, Mamiko, who has been in a persistent vegetative state since a road accident seven years ago.
chosen_option_text: “You know, all this was unnecessary,” muses Imogen Flanders, your ever-practical Minister of Solutions. “We should force everyone to decide what they want to happen in case of incapacity, while they’re young and compos mentis. If Mrs. Rodriguez had made a living will, everyone would have known her wishes, and there’d have been no legal battle. Also, had she not wanted to live in this tragic state, it would have saved the family and the insurance companies a lot of expensive medical bills. What? I’m just saying!”

title: Milking It
text: Vanilla Llaman consumers have seen the prices of dairy products continue to skyrocket, seemingly without reason. However, a recent exposé by an investigative journalist has finally shed light on this situation: the three largest dairy producers in Vanilla Llama have conspired to fix prices.
chosen_option_text: “What? Holy cow! We were just trying to, uh, help our farmers!” exclaims Curd Holstein, CEO of MooMoo Pure Dairy. “Supermarket price wars were driving milk rates so low that dairy farmers were running at a loss, and struggling to make ends meet. Our noble goal was to improve their lot by increasing the prices, but nobody appreciates us! You should support and congratulate us, Leader, as well as provide subsidies to the dairy industry.”

title: Immune Deficiencies
text: Hugo Iglesias, the spouse of a United Federation diplomat, was thrust into the spotlight when he drove on the wrong side of the road and struck 19-year-old motorcyclist Michelle Popov, killing her. Hugo then returned to his homeland quickly afterward, and — thanks to privileges extending to the families of diplomats — he is technically immune to prosecution.
chosen_option_text: “The problem is those twerps who run the UF are standing in the way of justice!” rages Michelle’s mother, Veda. “I say you show those fat foreign idiots who’s boss! Send commandos to grab this Iglesias man, and drag him here. You’ll be sending a message to other nations too, that no-one can escape Vanilla Llaman law!”

title: Leader to New Emu City: Drop Dead?
text: New Emu City is a semi-autonomous economically-important port city known for both its generous municipal welfare programs and its maverick mayor that’s long butted heads over your policies. After years of mounting financial problems, the city is on the verge of defaulting on its debts — which threatens to disrupt the national economy.
chosen_option_text: “I knew that this new-fangled ‘devolution’ experiment was a mistake,” scolds decrepit politician Ruby Leach, whose wheelchair and herself are gathering cobwebs. “Back in my day, when we controlled everything, all the cities and regions ran a tight ship on their finances. Now they spend, spend, spend like a flapper at a hootenanny! Revoke their right to set their budgets and place it in the hands of Vanilla Llama City, where it belongs. After all, no one knows better about the lives of those pastoral New Emuers than people like I. And another thing—” she abruptly falls asleep.

title: An Archaeological Altercation
text: During the construction of a new Hyper-Mega-Ultra-Super Mall, construction workers have unearthed what appears to be an ancient temple. A furious debate has arisen between those who wish to preserve it, and those who need their retail therapy.
chosen_option_text: “It’s all very nice to get to know some more about our past,” argues foreman Jim Gibson. “But that’s just the thing! It’s the past! We must think of the future. If you allow those decrepit fossils to take over this place, you put at risk the future of our economy! Today it’s archaeological digs, tomorrow it’s ‘preservation of the environment’. Just let me bulldoze the worthless pile of rubble and bury it under a few hundred tonnes of concrete.”

title: Don’t Burn Baby Don’t Burn
text: Yesterday, a house in Vanilla Llama City caught fire while two young children were inside. Firefighters rescued the children, who were found hiding from the flames in a closet, before it was too late.
chosen_option_text: “Children who are unfamiliar with fire instinctively hide from it,” says Fire Chief Modi, holding up a weighty fire safety manual titled Fires: They’re Not Lit. “We’ve even seen situations where kids have hidden from uniformed firefighters. You should add fire safety to the national curriculum and provide grants for fire departments to visit schools so that we can teach kids how to escape fires.”

title: Too Big to Rig
text: Accusations of bid-rigging have arisen after a company run by your brother, Tsewang, secured its fourth large government construction contract in a row. After dealing with weeks of complaints from good government advocates — and many impassioned pleas from Tsewang to ignore the issue — formal discussion about government contracting has reached your desk.
chosen_option_text: “Why do we bother working with those leeches?” bemoans Lucius Li, the head of an obscure maintenance department, who’s currently fixing a pipe in your office. “Why not just have the government do the work directly? It may be expensive to set up, but we won’t have to worry about who’s related to who or ingrates overcharging us, and we’ll create some good-paying jobs in the process. We all know you can always count on the government to deliver high-quality ser—” the pipe then sprays water in his face.

title: Please Don’t Feed the (Copyright) Trolls
text: Major film studio Werner Cousins recently began enforcing its copyright on the popular “Merry Birthday” song and has been demanding that everyone from schools, to small children, to your own government, pay royalties for its use. After one of the studio’s lawyers threatened to sue your secretary’s daughter for royalties, your government has finally agreed to address the issue of copyright trolling.
chosen_option_text: “Why should we deal with copyright at all?” suggests longtime political activist Red Foreman as he hands out copies of The Little Pinko Book to everyone in the room. “Nationalize the work of any author, including songs, movies, trademarks and even designs. Creativity is an important educational function, and the bourgeois copyright trolls have no right to censor it. Once the work is popular enough, it should be released into the public domain. Sure, some artists and creators might lose that financial incentive to create, but at least this copyright problem will be a thing of the past!”

title: Friends, Vanilla Llamen, Countrymen, Lend Me Your Ears
text: After the Citizenship and Immigration Services announced that they received a record number of applicants for naturalization, people have once again begun to debate who should or should not be considered Vanilla Llaman countrymen.
chosen_option_text: “Hey, that’s absolutely horrific!” hollers Themba Licorish, a Lilliputian immigrant. “Vanilla Llama needs to be open to all colors, creeds and cultures that come here to live a better life. Nothing justifies punishing people for having the ‘wrong’ birthplace or family tree. Everyone born in Vanilla Llama deserves the right for equal treatment! And even if you weren’t born here, it should be easy to join the ranks of your fellow citizens!”

title: The Meek Shall Inherit?
text: Wealthy slaveowner Pete Ungar has passed away, leaving behind several children who wish to divide his estate among themselves. Among them is Gertie Ungar, the daughter of Pete and one of his female slaves.
chosen_option_text: “Perhaps a compromise?” suggests peripatetic arbiter Bruno Räikkönen. “This woman’s mother was not a citizen, due to being a slave, but her father was free. Why don’t we declare the children of a slave and a free person as half-people? So they can be entitled to half the rights that free citizens enjoy, and Gertie can receive half a share in the inheritance. Problem solved.”

title: A Role to Play
text: Perpetual loner and social outcast Daveo Nixon made the news after holding five of his schoolmates hostage in a classroom for four hours, forcing them at sword-point (with an excellent replica Toledo Salamanca rapier) to play the popular role-playing game Trials and Trolls. Though everyone was released unharmed and the boy is now under arrest, many are asking if the game is a bad influence...
chosen_option_text: “People need to mind their own business,” states self-proclaimed nerd and ‘TnT-otaku’ Sun Clinton, proudly wearing a ‘Jesus Saves And Takes Half Damage’ t-shirt. “This is a positive activity, which can teach you social skills, maths, story-telling, and stuff! Sure, sometimes a player who has too much soda will fling half a dozen four-sided dice at someone’s head, because you know, magic missiles, ha-ha, but no real harm done by that. If this psycho held his fellow students hostage, it was because he was mentally ill, not because he gamed. Maybe deal with the mental health funding gap, and leave our hobby alone?”

title: Blood Type: Gay Positive
text: Carter Kettering, a young man prevented from donating much-needed blood because of his sexuality, has been on a media blitz after popular queer magazine Out! picked up and disseminated the story. With the newscycle being dominated by the topic, your inundated press office has requested you come to a decision on what to do. In that vein, you’ve called all parties to the case to your office.
chosen_option_text: “But the LORD sayeth YOU SHALLETH NOT prick the finger of THE GAYETH because you might becometh GAYETH yourself. Eth!” shouts Zuko Fawlty, representative of some faith groups within Vanilla Llama. “The gays want to donate blood to infect everyone with their gayness! Don’t let that happen, Leader. Not only do we need to ban gays from giving blood, we need to ban them, PERIOD! For the people. DO ITETH in the name of the LORDETH!”

title: Baby Shower
text: The number of pregnant tourists arriving in Vanilla Llama dramatically increased after the country started granting citizenship to all babies born on its soil. Several of your sources report that most of these birth tourists are wealthy and often come from authoritarian nations.
chosen_option_text: “Let’s not be too hasty here,” chimes in Mia Nahasapeemapetilon, your chief financial adviser, scribbling some numbers on a sheet of paper. “Don’t you realize what a lucrative business opportunity we have here? If these parents are willing to spend lots of money to travel here just so their kids can be citizens, maybe we should charge them for each baby born in Vanilla Llama! You know, like a citizenship tax. According to my calculations, this would fill up our coffers in no time!”

title: The Making of a Mass Murderer
text: Seemingly with nothing better to do with their time, the Ministry of Statistics has conducted a study profiling the most prolific Vanilla Llaman serial killers and murderers. They have determined that the vast majority of the perpetrators tend to be sexually frustrated single men.
chosen_option_text: “I think maybe our report isn’t being taken as a whole,” drones Ministry Statistician Jean-Paul Bowman in a dull monotone. “Correlations with lack of sexual satisfaction exist, but there’s also low educational attainment, social isolation, childhood trauma, association with sexually deviant communities, lack of stable employment and the Hervey Cleckley ‘Mask of Sanity’ to consider. You know what would really help? More funding for the Ministry of Statistics, and a pay rise for your statisticians. I mean, sometimes, I get so frustrated about the lack of security in this lonely job. I know I should have studied harder, I just wanted to make mother proud but she always wanted more... always so much more...” He trails off and stares into space for a while.

title: Champagne in the Glass
text: Overnight, police in Vanilla Llama City raided dozens of stores selling counterfeit wine that was masquerading as vintages from Vanilla Llama, but actually originated from Dàguó. Furious wine executives and other lobbyists have pressed into your office the following day, afroth with rage.
chosen_option_text: “Our friend from the winery has an excellent idea. After all, bureaucracy solves everything,” chimes in red-tape lover Norm Gumble, who was reportedly voted ‘most likely to correct your grammar’ during high school. “Let’s take it a step further: nationalize all alcohol sales in Vanilla Llama under the LLO brand. We can then control the product coming in, have enormous buying power, and rake in a vat load of taxes to help our ailing coffers. It’s a tipple, er, triple win! Cheers!”

title: Cloudy With a Chance of Fecal Matter
text: Last night’s spectacular meteor shower was actually something far less celestial: “space peanuts,” solidified clumps of human excrement ejected from passenger aircraft.
chosen_option_text: “Seems to me that you should blame the fool who didn’t go at the airport,” declares your great-great-grandmother, who recently escaped her care facility and is now rocking gently in your office. “The solution’s simple: ban pooping on planes. If they didn’t think ahead and relieve themselves before they stepped foot on their flight, they can suffer the consequences. And as the saying goes: you can’t make a poop meteor without the poop.”

title: No Country for Old Men
text: After several incidents which resulted in the loss of millions of marks have been discovered to be caused by senility and feebleness, concerned financial and medical professionals are wondering if retirement should be made mandatory at a certain age.
chosen_option_text: “It’s not really such a bad idea,” suggests Efthamia McCarthy, your middle-aged medical adviser while checking your pulse to see if you’re still alive. “You see, when some people reach a certain age, they become too weak and mentally incompetent to do their job. Therefore, we need to impose mandatory retirement so our nation wouldn’t have to put up with things like that senile 95-year-old rickshaw driver who caused that day-long traffic jam on the highway. Of course, we mustn’t be cruel: we should also provide better pensions for them so they’ll be content in their dotage.”

title: Culture Wars
text: A family from Vanilla Llama was arrested while on holiday in Tasmania for taking a photo of their child urinating in Lake Sacred - a cultural icon that is revered by all Tasmanians. This incident, and others of Vanilla Llamen behaving badly while abroad, has resulted in a national debate about how uncivilized Vanilla Llama appears to the rest of Land of Faceplace.
chosen_option_text: “We are the laughing stock of Land of Faceplace,” opines your mother, as she picks up the litter on the floor of your office. “We need to draw up a list of government-sanctioned guidelines to show Vanilla Llamen how to behave properly in the countries they are visiting, and require that all travel agents hand over a copy to anyone who books a foreign holiday. We need to understand that, although some Vanilla Llamen urinate in fountains and throw rubbish everywhere here, it is not acceptable in other countries.”

title: Tinder Profiled
text: Predictions of an unusually cold upcoming winter and a nostalgic trend towards old-fashioned home comforts have seen a spike in the number of fireplace installations, which are increasingly recognised as having significant health and environmental impacts.
chosen_option_text: “Whilst we’re at it, we should be banning oil and gas heaters in all newly constructed buildings as well. They’re bad, so bad, you know it,” adds his companion, a pop star famous for his eco-conscious hit single ‘Mud Song’. “There’s plenty of other ways to keep warm indoors: air and ground source heat pumps, thermally passive buildings, or just wearing more clothes. If we want to make the world a better place, we gotta look at the man in the mirror, and make a change.”

title: The Issue With Issues
text: After an influx of poorly thought out, redundant, and otherwise trivial issues have been shoved across your desk, concern has been raised as to whether the government should start better regulating the issues you receive.
chosen_option_text: You suddenly hear a shattering noise and find Cooper Bourdain, your Advisor Of Trivial Matters, has broken through your office window. “Sorry about that, your office door was being fixed,” he apologizes. “Anyway, an issues crackdown? Ha! Your window’s a trivial issue, yet you’ll probably be enlisting all of Vanilla Llama’s government to replace it! I say, anyone who wants should be able to bring an issue directly to your attention! Then the people will feel like the government is a helpful organization working for them, not something big to fear! If that doesn’t work, I’ll even help fix your window!”

title: Students Demand Financial Aid
text: Students from many universities in Vanilla Llama are protesting about the rising financial cost of studying at university and are demanding that the government provide more financial aid to students.
chosen_option_text: “These young people are the greatest resource our nation has,” says Jeffrey Pond, a famous demographer. “If you’re going to discourage them from going to university then you’re cheating our nation out of its potential. What I suggest is government-funded loans to students from poor families. That way we can have the best of both worlds without the expense. Admittedly, some may still not be able to afford it but there’s no pleasing some people.”

title: It’s a Girl Thing
text: A commercial for a new childrenswear boutique has been unveiled, sparking debate over gender stereotypes in advertising. It features a young girl ballet-dancing in a rose-pink bedroom, holding a baby-pink toy unicorn and a fluffy cameo-pink magic wand, while wearing matching cotton-candy pink dancing shoes, a tiara and flounced pink tutu.
chosen_option_text: “The impact of ads can be used to our advantage,” states your Minister of Niceness Sage Rifkin, tutting disapprovingly at Ms. Cox, who is still writing anatomical suggestions of where you might stick the vacuum. “Pay financial incentives to advertisers who depict Vanilla Llamen in stereotype-shattering roles, so society will become more open-minded. Imagine: women playing exhausting sports, toasting friends in a coffee shop, wiring a plug, administering a company, even growing a beard. And men, too long derided as incompetent homemakers, unafraid to nurture a baby in public, tend a sick parent, or cook a meal. Break antiquated gender roles and protect your citizens’ freedom!”

title: A Bone to Pick
text: Acclaimed yet controversial thespian Ichabod Amin elicited shock (and not coincidentally, more than a little publicity) after performing Hamlet with the severed head of his recently deceased uncle taking the role of ‘Yorick’ in lieu of the usual fake skull. A debate has begun over proper respect for human remains, and whether the general public should be allowed to own them.
chosen_option_text: “DAH-ling, when I play the Oedipal Prince I want your rapt attention!” explains the pretentious actor, shaking his uncle’s left femur at you for emphasis. “Did not the jester’s head held aloft in my hand both capture and captivate your gaze? Was I not momentarily a solitary tableau vivant to behold and admire? A replica would have lacked authenticity, and the Art demands authenticity! Owning human bones should be perfectly legal for all, as should gathering any unclaimed remains. My wondrous panoply of accoutrements is not complete without these fragments of mortality!”

title: Welfare Programs Not Faring Well
text: A recent lull in legislation has sparked the fires of some bored politicians. After reviewing the back-log of constituent complaints, they’ve come to your desk demanding welfare reform.
chosen_option_text: “Capitalism is the very reason why we need welfare in the first place. Laissez-faire policies would only make the problem worse,” argues political activist Heidi Belcher. “If the government took control of all businesses, it could ensure that all employees are paid the amount they need to live - no more, no less - then the problem of providing for the poor would disappear.”

title: The Queen in Yellow
text: An undergraduate medical statistician has stumbled across a weird occurrence: three of the five actors involved in a theatrical piece called The Queen in Yellow, as well as over ten percent of the members of the opening night audience, have since received diagnoses of various psychiatric illnesses. The media have picked up on this, labelling it “the play that sends you mad”, and predictably ticket sales are now skyrocketing.
chosen_option_text: “Selective reporting!” shouts mathematics professor Camilla Whateley. “It’s like when they claimed that fighter jet pilots were having more female children, all over again. You need to learn how selection bias and basic statistics work. More to the point, the nation needs to learn how these things work. I’d suggest making stats a compulsory part of a properly funded core school curriculum. 85.7% of the seven statisticians I surveyed agree this is a good idea. The other guy, he’s just an annoying smelly little...”

title: They Took Our Gubment!
text: Vanilla Llama City media has been abuzz with gossip that Harold Weissenegger, a former bodybuilder and action movie star turned politician who immigrated from Smalltopia at a young age, is set to run for Parliament in the upcoming election. With Weissenegger already ahead in early polls, the legality of an immigrant running for office has been brought into question.
chosen_option_text: “I live here, work here, pay taxes here... well I live here,” monologues Mr Weissenegger after smashing your door down for dramatic effect. “So there’s no problemo with me running for office.” As he tramples out of the splintered doorway, his last words are carried to you: “Or I’ll be back.”

title: Scouting for Boys, Girls... Anyone?
text: The Vanilla Llaman Scouts, a volunteer youth group that teaches boys and girls outdoor survival skills, are reporting sharply declining numbers. The organization’s annual meet was attended by just seven and a half Scouts (as there was an unfortunate accident involving a canoe made out of recycled soup cans). Some within the community are urging the government to help revive interest in outdoor pursuits among young people.
chosen_option_text: “All this tradition stuff is exactly why kids aren’t interested in Scouting anymore,” snarks your appallingly cynical niece, who only looks up from her phone to roll her eyes. “What use are badges for campfire building and map reading when we have central heating and GPS? If Scouting taught some more modern skills, maybe you’d have more young people interested.”

title: No, Minister
text: The recently published memoirs of a retired senior civil servant have caused an uproar with their claims that it is the Civil Service, not the government, that runs the country.
chosen_option_text: “Shocking, leader, shocking,” murmurs civil servant Humphrey Pearby. “I absolutely agree with you about the Civil Service, and understand your instructions perfectly! I will immediately establish a Department of Civil Service Budget Oversight Committee for the Investigation of Pecuniary Distribution. Leave it to me, I will get the ball rolling, immediately! That is what you are saying isn’t it? Yes, Minister?”

title: Vanilla Llamen Still Footing the Bill
text: Capitalizing on your office hours today, industrious Vanilla Llamen have monopolized your desk space with a series of medical bills, lamenting that despite Vanilla Llama’s proudly socialized economy, the government still doesn’t provide universal healthcare.
chosen_option_text: “Universal healthcare would be a relief, but hospitals and doctors’ offices need (cough) room to breathe,” asserts Ash the Asthmatic Architect, desperately searching for his inhaler among a mess of blueprints. “The countryside has plenty of open space, trees and fields for construction crews, just inhale environmental funds and exhale red cro- (cough) crosses instead. All that green is what’s turning patients blue.”

title: What a Gneiss Place We’ve Got Here
text: A vast and seemingly endless new cave system has just been discovered in a remote section of Violetstone National Park! Despite not even having a name yet, petitioners are crowding your office telling you what to do with it.
chosen_option_text: “Whoop-dee-doo, there’s a new cave! Get over it,” snorts Shelia Nakatomi, one of Violetstone’s junior rangers. “You know what else is still there? Any number of trees, flowers, bunnies — you name it — all happily undisturbed by human activities. I say we keep it that way with a boost to the park budget. With more money, we can crack down on anyone who tries to illegally enter prohibited areas.”

title: A Slip of the Tongue
text: The nation — or at least, some part of it — is in mourning after the death of Nefertiti Fernandez, the last speaker of an obscure language native to the far-flung hinterlands of Vanilla Llama. Only the most recent in a decades-long trend of native linguistic extinctions, Fernandez’s death has spurred a motley association of concerned parties to petition for something to be done.
chosen_option_text: “Alas, poor Nefertiti!” laments the linguist Uther Márquez. “I did not know her, Leader. Nor anything about her language actually, but that’s besides the point. This is not the first language that has died on our watch nor will it be the last. There are hundreds of endangered languages within the borders of Vanilla Llama, and who knows how long it’ll be before they too are gone! You must fund the efforts of our linguists to go out and make records of these languages from what speakers remain before it’s too late! Did you know that the Ouron tribespeople have over 50 different words for urine? It’s simply fascinating, and so we must preserve their profound insights.”

title: Solving a Dissolving Dilemma
text: Following several months of political squabbling, there is concern that the incumbent legislature in Vanilla Llama is no longer able to function efficiently. As a result, some have been questioning if voters should be allowed to dissolve the parliament and call for a new election.
chosen_option_text: “This is obviously an absurd notion,” says Mohandas Sims, the current Minister of the Interior. “Vanilla Llama has had a regular election schedule for ages, without any major catastrophes since that incident with Mr. Scruffy. There’s no need to muck it up by constantly dissolving parliament. The voters elected us for a full term of office; to serve anything less than that is anti-democratic.”

title: Genetics Brings New Life to Extinct Species
text: Scientists have announced they are close to a breakthrough in their quest to revive the feather-bellied emu, a species related to Vanilla Llama’s national animal that has been extinct for more than a century.
chosen_option_text: “Now, come on,” says Reignbeau Miller, well-known philosopher. “You don’t need to believe in some outside force to be unnerved by the top of this particular slippery slope. Today it’s emus, tomorrow it’s dinosaurs, and we all know how that turns out. This research shouldn’t be banned, but there must be strict government controls over its use.”

title: Ghost Riders on the Sly
text: Following the passage of a well-supported bill that contained half a dozen riders, corruption watchdog groups are lobbying the government to take action against the use of these unrelated addenda in lawmaking.
chosen_option_text: “Yes, these riders can be a threat to the democratic process,” begins Party Majority Leader Slartibartfast Smit. “But to ban them outright is simply foolish. We need the ability to amend bills, and sometimes those attachments aren’t always clearly connected. Therefore, I propose we grant the legislature the ability to veto any rider by a simple majority vote. That way, necessary riders can still be attached and this other tom-foolery can be nipped in the bud.”

title: May I Pick Your Brain?
text: A recent exposé has revealed that the wealthy Kennadoof family sent one of their more rebellious daughters to an institution where her brain’s frontal lobe was cut, in a way that destroyed her higher brain functions. She was subsequently hidden from public sight for years. This procedure, called ‘lobotomy’, remains legal in Vanilla Llama. The resulting public backlash has caused quite a headache for your government.
chosen_option_text: “What this ‘activist’ fails to address is that lobotomies can be medically useful,” counters Declan Fowler, director of the Vanilla Llama City Institute for the Demented, shoving a little boy in front of you. “Just look at little Timmy here: his OCD has been completely cured! Plenty of our patients live better lives after they are cured of their ailments. As such, we need to make sure lobotomies are used for all cases where the unruly and unwell might benefit!”

title: Fantastic Beasts and How Vanilla Llama Harmed Them
text: A shocking exposé on tourist attraction OceanWorld has revealed the mistreatment of captive orcas and other marine animals. Your office has since faced a tidal wave of complaints demanding government action.
chosen_option_text: “Perhaps there could be a compromise?” queries your Minister of the Environment, Belinda Fforde, who has been smelling like grass lately. “Ending zoos would harm the tourism industry, and we can’t deny that these programs help endangered species. Why don’t we set a limit on what animals they take? Specifically the endangered ones? I’m sure that we can also force tougher standards to ensure OceanWorld treats the animals humanely as well.”

title: Bunged Up
text: Calamity in the Emu Canal! An exceptionally large container ship called the ‘Never Taken’ has run aground in one of the nation’s most vital shipping passages. Stormy weather, tight schedules and the captain’s overconfidence have been variously suggested as the cause. Regardless, the ship is now wedged at an angle across the canal, blocking the passage of other cargo vessels.
chosen_option_text: “Uh huh, and what if it all hits the fan again?” says Henny Ma, your Minister of Health, sipping on a tall glass of prune juice. “Prevention is better than cure, and we can prevent little accidents in the future by ensuring regular movements. Clear the path, for sure, but then invest the ten or twenty billion marks needed to widen and deepen the canal walls.”

title: Bye Bye to the Birdies?
text: After Smalltopian journalists reporting on recent protein powder trade negotiations penned more articles on Vanilla Llaman government buildings covered in bird droppings than international commerce, questions have been raised as to whether Vanilla Llama’s “pigeon problem” has gotten out of control.
chosen_option_text: “This is their city as much as it is ours,” sings your childhood nanny Miriam Poppout, while staring at a snow globe with unsettling intensity. “You can’t let these beautiful creatures die! We should embrace bird feeding. Vanilla Llama City will become known as ‘The City of a Million Pigeons’ and tourists will flock from across the world to see the birds and feed them at only two marks a bag.”

title: Demonic Possession Getting You Down?
text: Reports that more and more Vanilla Llamen are seeking exorcisms for being possessed by evil spirits are fuelling rumours of an impending apocalypse.
chosen_option_text: Finally, a man dressed in a dark suit and holding a pile of contracts seems to appear out of nowhere. “I am from the law firm Horace, Edward, Logan and Lee. My client has instructed me to inform you that there is only one way to save the Vanilla Llaman people from this calamity. Tell all of them to sign these contracts, then my client shall transport them all to a place far away from the imminent catastrophe. There’s nothing to be suspicious about, my client is a reasonable fellow.”

title: Bicameral Backlash
text: The Vanilla Llaman upper house recently voted down a major tourism bill, provoking significant backlash in the lower house. Legislators have gathered in your office, and they’re now debating whether Vanilla Llama truly needs an upper house.
chosen_option_text: “The old woman is right,” comments Melania Delauter, the head of the Vanilla Llaman Electoral Commission. “Our nation needs an upper house to be a check on the lower. After all, unicameralism would basically make you an elected dictator with all that unchecked power. At the same time, the upper house’s disapproval should not be a death knell for otherwise popular legislation. I have a compromise. Let’s allow the lower house to call a snap election if the upper house blocks one of its bills. If the lower house, after the election, passes the same bill again, then it becomes law regardless of what the upper legislators think. Expensive? Sure, but at least we give the people the right to break parliamentary stalemates whenever they happen.”

title: Edged Out
text: Banning guns has reduced gun crime, but in its place knife crime is rising. A recent anonymous survey of teenagers suggests that a frighteningly high proportion of them carry a blade routinely.
chosen_option_text: “A knife is a vital tool!” exclaims outdoorsman Amir Gibson, using his Bowie knife to peel a banana. “Responsible adults like me shouldn’t be punished! Just ban blade ownership till the age of majority; let grown-ups carry whatever blades they need to. Ouch!” He yelps as he nicks his finger.

title: Can I Borrow a Word?
text: A group of disgruntled language connoisseurs are complaining that loan-words from the Galliennais language are ‘contaminating the native tongue of Vanilla Llama’. They are calling for a government sponsored language purification project, robbing you of your joie de vivre as you try to relax and enjoy your pamplemousse cocktail.
chosen_option_text: “Oh mon dieu, but this approach will not work, as it doesn’t target the raison d’être for Galliennais loan-words,” enunciates William Norman, an enthusiastic Galliennais Literature professor from Cambarry University, with visible ennui. “The Galliennais culture is superior to ours, and so is their langue, par conséquent we need Galliennais words to express high-brow concepts such as rapprochement, savoir-faire, and je ne sais quoi. The importation of Galliennais words is fait accompli, and trying to reverse this will only be a faux pas. Let us embrace and teach to all Galliennais words and linguistic diversity: vive la différence!”

title: Size Matters
text: Historically, the broad international consensus has always been to use the Maxcator Projection to depict the world on flat maps. The downside is that this projection makes Vanilla Llama look disproportionately small, as well as tucking it away on the edge of the map. After a recent TV drama made this a hot topic, disgruntled patriots are pressing you for a government stance on this.
chosen_option_text: “The world? The world that matters ends at our national borders!” proclaims a cigar-smoking man in the shadows. “You should be encouraging people to stay at home and to work for our nation, not to worry about foreign lands. You must only allow the publication of maps up to our national borders. In fact, stop our citizens leaving the country at all: if they never see the outside world, they won’t worry why others have things that they don’t.”

title: Ten Days in a Mad House
text: Investigative journalist Agatha Ryan has published a damning critique of Vanilla Llama’s mental health facilities after spending ten days undercover as a psychiatric patient in Vanilla Llama City State Asylum. Her report details abuse, incompetence and negligence, and has led to angry clamors for reform of how the system is managed.
chosen_option_text: “These hospitals are being run like prisons!” belts irate social worker Matthias Assange as he slams down a copy of the article on your desk. “Patients are treated like inmates; their rooms are like cells, and these antiquated ‘treatments’ redefine barbaric! Something must be done!” He pauses for a moment to regain his composure. “We need to completely revamp the state of mental health treatment in this country. Let’s start by convening a meeting of all the world’s leading psychiatrists - put up at our expense, of course - and then build a new specialist care facility in every town in Vanilla Llama.”

title: The Fault in Our Skyline
text: Following a speech at the annual Vanilla Llaman Urban Planning Conference, several attendees cornered you to discuss national zoning laws. These laws prohibit almost all middle-density development, including mid-rises, small apartment buildings, and other infrastructure which provide lower-cost housing and a stronger sense of community.
chosen_option_text: “We’ve plenty of land if we’re willin’ to venture outside y’all’s big cities,” notes Wangdi Baker, a petite person chewing on a piece of straw who gave a talk earlier in the conference on rural development. “Our rural and suburban townships got so much room, we’re rolling in them hills! If y’allow us to expand our residential zones - and maybe slide us hamlets some extra marks - we’ll create a bungalow paradise that will be the envy of all our countrymen. We may not have elitist luxuries like ‘job opportunities’ just yet but we got twice the heart those city folk got, and if you support our development, I guarantee y’all that Vanilla Llamen will flock to our community!”

title: Do You Think He’s Overcompensating for Something?
text: Larger and heavier cars have proliferated in recent years. These have been linked to higher fatality rates after collisions with pedestrians and smaller vehicles, as well as causing traffic problems on narrower roads.
chosen_option_text: “Some of us own normal sedan cars, and are sick of finding ourselves hemmed in on all sides by tanks,” complains a nervous looking man, who is wearing a shirt two sizes too small. “I accept that industry and workmen need trucks, but is it sensible for the average commuter to be taking up all this road space? Surely you can at least ban them for normal non-business drivers, and maybe also restrict the installation of unnecessary lift kits, bull bars, and other after-market modifications that make a large vehicle bigger and more unsafe for everyone else outside of it.”

title: Pensioners in Protest
text: Falling standards at the retirement homes of Vanilla Llama have prompted OAPs to take to the streets and demand better treatment.
chosen_option_text: “There needs to be more done for the elderly,” says Theresa Atwood, a resident of ‘This Old Man’ retirement home. “We can’t work to support ourselves anymore, and the pensions we get are measly. We need more benefits such as higher standards of living, free bus tickets, and a continuous supply of marks. All it requires is a little more generosity on the part of the tax payers - after all, we fought the war for their sort.”

title: A Salt and Battery
text: Electric cars have vastly reduced air pollution in Vanilla Llama. However, this has accompanied a surge in demand for lithium, a scarce element primarily obtained through heavy mining. As lithium salts are a critical component in electric vehicle batteries, your advisers fear a shortage could cripple electric car manufacturers and the Vanilla Llaman lifestyle.
chosen_option_text: “Lithium-ion batteries power tons of often-tossed electronics,” yaps Vanilla Llama City-area sanitation director Johann Christmas, who is wearing a T-shirt with the slogan ‘Garbage In, Treasure Out’. “We can reuse that lithium if we expand recycling infrastructure to accommodate the extra rubbish. Now look, this garbage idea has a catch — lithium recycling can’t beat mining in terms of output — so there’d be less of the stuff to go around. However, if we reduced lithium demand by hiking taxes on automobiles and electronics while also encouraging use of mass transit, we’d be able to make it work.”

title: Animal Experimentation Laws Under Scrutiny
text: Scientists and animal rights activists have once again brought up the debate over animal experimentation to your attention.
chosen_option_text: “It is not unethical,” replies Dr. Falala Hammarskjöld, the chief surgeon at Vanilla Llama’s largest cancer research clinic. “The unethical thing to do would be to deny the public of the benefit of the great scientific advancements we’re making! If we have to sacrifice some animals in the name of science, healthcare, or slightly prettier eyeliner, then that’s just what we’ve got to do! Think of the lives we could save! All we require is more government support and funding for this worthy cause.”

title: Better In Than Out
text: Your Justice Minister has raised a stink about public flatulence, and is proposing a new law to ban it.
chosen_option_text: “This is insane,” states Jasper McDuck, your Solicitor General, discreetly shifting in his chair. “How any reasonable or sensible person could think that criminalizing flatulence in public would be a good idea is beyond me. We are a civilized nation. Just make sure that everyone is taught to do it as discreetly as possible when they need to. Simply raise your right buttock ever so slightly and let it out gently, ideally without bringing any attention to yourself.”

title: The Dialectics of Dialects
text: A few days ago, a tourist from Brancaland was hospitalized due to a severe allergic reaction after ingesting street food in Emu City. It turned out he had asked the local vendor about the ingredients, but had been unable to understand her heavily accented reply. The incident has stirred up a debate over what to do about the wildly different dialects of Vanilla Llama.
chosen_option_text: “Och, awa’ ye go wi’ that rubbish!” scoffs Danni McKinnon, a resident of a city in the far north of Vanilla Llama. “We dinnae need tae be panderin’ tae yon tourists; if they cannae understaund wit it is we’re saying, then dae ye really think they shid be comin’ here tae begin with?” She taps her head with a finger. “Think on, Leader, think on.”

title: Burning Over a New Leaf
text: Many Vanilla Llamen have long equated the autumn with colder temperatures, apple bobbing, pumpkin spice, and the aromatic tradition of burning fallen leaves to avoid doing yard work. Although the smoky scents of burning foliage are soothing to some, an uptick in the number of domestic fires caused by immolating leaf piles has lead to a growing call to ban the hallowed practice.
chosen_option_text: “Jeez, this all sounds like so much work,” groans the boyfriend of your fourth cousin, thrice-removed, Vinnie ‘Fun’ Guy, who gives his occupation as ‘waste management’. “These leaves causing problems? Why not just take out the source? Cut down a few trees, bada-bing bada-boom, no more leaves sticking their veins where they ain’t wanted, causing honest folks to start fires. I know a guy who owes me. We’ll take care of this problem for ya. Want us to make it look like an accident?”

title: It’s UterUs, Not UterYou!
text: A religious talk show host raised a furor with his call to ban contraception. Women’s rights groups have come to you demanding a response.
